translations.text: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar, the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah,
the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar. The hand of the Lord was upon me there.

I looked, and there was a storm wind coming from the north, a great cloud, and blazing fire shining all around it. From within it, from within the fire, there was something like the appearance of [?].
Within it was the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they resembled human beings.
Each had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight, and the hooves of their feet were like calves’ hooves. They gleamed like shining bronze.
There were human hands beneath their wings on their four sides, and their faces and their wings were on their sides.
Their wings touched one another. When they moved, they went straight ahead without turning.
Their faces resembled human faces, with lion faces on their right sides, and ox faces and eagle faces on their left sides.
Their faces and wings were spread out above. Two wings touched one another, and two covered their bodies.
They went straight ahead, wherever the spirit went, without turning.
The living creatures resembled burning coals of fire, like the appearance of a torch moving among the living creatures. The fire shone brightly, and lightning came out of it.
The living creatures ran without turning back, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
I looked at the living creatures, and there were wheels on the ground beside all four living creatures.
The appearance and construction of the wheels were like the appearance of beryl. All four had the same likeness, and their appearance and construction were like a wheel within a wheel.
They moved in any of their four directions without turning. Wherever their front turned to go, they followed it without turning.
Their rims were high, and they could see. The rims of all four were full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them, and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them.
Wherever the spirit went, they went, and the wheels rose with them, because a living spirit was in the wheels.
When they moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, because a living spirit was in the wheels.
Stretched out above the heads of the living creatures was something resembling awe-inspiring crystal.
Beneath it, their wings were stretched straight toward one another. Above and below, two covered them, and two covered their bodies.

I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of mighty waters and like the voice of God when they moved, and like the sound of speech within a camp. When they stood still, they quieted their wings.
There was a voice above the canopy over their heads. When they stood still, they quieted their wings.
Above the canopy over their heads was something like a sapphire stone in appearance, resembling a throne. Above the likeness of the throne was a figure resembling a human being.

I saw something like the appearance of God, and something like fire within, all around him, from the appearance of his waist upward. From his waist downward I saw something like fire, and brightness surrounded him.

Like the appearance of a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the appearance of the brightness surrounding him. Such was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. When I saw it, I fell facedown and heard the voice of someone speaking.
And he said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you.”
The spirit entered me as he spoke with me and set me on my feet, and I heard him speaking with me.
He said to me, “Son of man, I am sending you to the people of Israel, to a rebellious people who have rebelled against me. They and their ancestors have sinned against me to this very day.
I am sending you to children whose faces are defiant and whose hearts are stubborn. Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says.’
Perhaps they will listen and tremble, for they are a rebellious household, and they will know that you are a prophet among them.

But you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or be alarmed by their words, though they reject and despise you, for you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or be alarmed by their faces, for they are a rebellious household.
But speak my words to them. Perhaps they will listen and tremble, for they are a rebellious household.
But you, son of man, listen to what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like the rebellious household. Instead, open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
I looked, and there was a hand stretched out toward me, holding a scroll.
He unrolled it before me. It had writing on the front and the back, and written on it were lamentations, reflections, and dirges.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go and speak to the house of Israel.”
I opened my mouth, and he fed me that scroll.
He said to me, “Son of man, fill your stomach and your bowels with this scroll that I am giving you.” I ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
He said to me, “Son of man, go to the exiles, to the people of Israel, and speak my words to them.
For I have not sent you to a people whose speech is obscure and whose language is foreign, but to the house of Israel.
Nor have I sent you to many peoples whose speech you do not understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
But the house of Israel will not listen to you, because they are unwilling to listen to me. For the whole house of Israel has a stubborn forehead and a hard heart.
Look, I have made your face hard against their faces, and I have made your forehead firm against their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or be alarmed in their presence, for they are a rebellious household.”
He said to me, “Son of man, take to heart all my words that I speak to you, and listen with your ears.
Go to the exiles, to your own people, and speak with them. Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says.’ Perhaps they will listen and tremble.”
The spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling, saying, “Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his place!”
There was the sound of the wings of the living creatures striking against one another, the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
The Spirit lifted me up and carried me away, and I went in the heat of my spirit, with the hand of the Lord strong upon me.
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib [?], who lived by the River Chebar, and I sat there among them for seven days, stunned.
After seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel, so that you may hear words from my mouth and warn them on my behalf.

When I say to a sinner, ‘You will certainly die,’ and you do not warn him or tell the sinner to turn from his way and live, that sinner will die in his wrongdoing, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the sinner and he does not turn from his sin and his evil way, he will die in his sins, but you will save your own life.

When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, I will put a stumbling block before him, and he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die in his sins, and the righteousness he practiced will not be remembered in his favor. But I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, the righteous person will live because he heeded the warning, and you will save your own life.”
The hand of the Lord came upon me there, and he said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
I got up and went out to the plain, and there stood the glory of the God of Israel, like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar. I fell on my face.
The Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said to me, “Go inside and shut yourself in your house.
As for you, son of man, look: they will put chains on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be speechless and unable to rebuke them, because they are a rebellious household.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, so that you may say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen, and whoever trembles, let him tremble, because they are a rebellious household.
Now you, son of man, take a brick, set it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.
Lay siege to it, build siege towers against it, set ambushes against it, pitch camps against it, and set up siege equipment all around it.
Take an iron pan and set it as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Set your face against it; it will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
Lie on your left side and place the wrongdoing of the house of Israel upon it. You will bear their wrongdoing for the number of days you lie on it.
I have assigned you the two sets of wrongdoing for a number of days: three hundred and ninety days. You will bear the wrongdoing of the house of Israel.
When you finish these, lie on your right side and bear the wrongdoing of the house of Judah for forty days. I have assigned you one day for each year.
Set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, strengthen your arm, and prophesy against it.
Look, I have put chains on you, and you will not turn from one side to the other until the days of your confinement are complete.

Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, put them in one container, and make bread for yourself from them. Eat it for the number of days you lie on your side: three hundred and ninety days.
Your food will be twenty shekels a day, eaten at set intervals.
You will drink water by measure, one-sixth of a hemina. You will drink it at set intervals.
You will eat a barley cake baked over human dung before their eyes.
The Lord said, “This is how the people of Israel will eat their bread in uncleanness among the nations where I will drive them.”
And I said, “God, Lord of lords, I have never been defiled. From my youth until today, I have not eaten a diseased animal or one torn apart by wild animals, and no unclean meat has entered my mouth.”
He said to me, “Look, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung, so that you may bake your bread over it.”
He said to me, “Son of man, look, I am cutting off the supply of grain in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight, and in their thirst they will drink water by measure.”
“They will lack bread and water, and they will perish together, each with his brother, and waste away because of their wrongdoing.”
But you, son of man, take a sword as sharp as a barber’s razor, and pass it over your head and your beard. Take weighing scales and divide the hair into three portions.

“Burn one of the three portions in the fire inside the city when the days of your confinement are completed. Take another portion and cut it with a sword around the city. Scatter the third portion in the wind, and a sword will bring destruction after them.”
“Take a few of them and tie them in the edge of your garment.”
“Then take some of these, throw them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From them a fire will spread against the whole house of Israel.”
This is what the Lord of lords says: “This is Jerusalem. I placed her among the nations, with all the cities surrounding her.”
“She has violated my judgments more sinfully than the nations, and my commandments more than the cities surrounding her, because they rejected my judgments and did not follow my commandments.”

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: “Because you have plotted more than the nations around you, and have not followed my commandments or carried out my judgments, but have carried out the judgments of the nations around you,”
therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: “Look, I myself am against you, and I will execute judgments within you in the sight of all the nations.”
“Because of all your uncleanness, I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again.”
“Therefore fathers will eat their children within you, and children will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter those who remain within you to every wind.”

“Therefore, as I live,” says the Lord of lords, “because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your filthy practices and all your uncleanness, I too will drive you away. My eye will not pity you, and I will show no mercy.”

“One portion of your people will die of pestilence and perish from famine within you. Another will fall by the sword around you. The third I will scatter to every wind, and a sword will bring destruction after them.”
“I will fully expend my anger and satisfy my fury against them, and I will be comforted. They will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my zeal when I have fully expended my anger against them.”
“I will make you a ruin and an object of disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.”

“You will become an object of disgrace and scorn, a warning and a cause of astonishment among the nations around you, when I execute judgments against you in anger, fury, and rebuke. I, the Lord, have spoken.”
“When I send against you my deadly arrows of famine, which bring destruction, I will send them to destroy you. I will increase the famine against you and cut off your supply of grain.”
“I will send famine and savage beasts against you and destroy you. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring a sword against you. I, the Lord, have spoken.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.”

“Say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord of lords. This is what the Lord of lords says to the mountains, hills, valleys, and ravines: Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your shrines.’”
“Your altars will be laid waste, your idols will be broken, and I will throw your slain down before the objects of your worship.”
I will cast the corpses of the house of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

“The cities throughout all the places where you live will be ruined, and the shrines will be laid waste, so that your altars will be ruined and desolate, your idols will be broken and brought to nothing, your carved images will be cut down, and the things you have made will be wiped out.”
“The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the Lord.”
I will leave some of you among the nations, those who escaped the sword and were scattered among the cities.

Those of you who escaped will remember me among the nations where they were taken captive, when I have broken their adulterous hearts that turned away from me, and their eyes that wandered after their idols. Their faces will grimace at the evil they have done and at all their uncleanness.
They will know that I am the Lord, and that I did not speak in vain when I said I would bring this disaster upon them.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and say, ‘Alas for all the uncleanness and wickedness of the house of Israel! They will fall by the sword, famine, and plague.’
Those who are far away will die of plague, and those who are near will fall by the sword. Those who remain and escape will die of famine, and I will fully carry out my wrath against them.

They will know that I am the Lord when their slain lie among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, beneath all the mountaintops, under every tree that gives shade, and under every leafy terebinth, in the places where they offered incense to all their idols.
I will raise my hand against them and make the land a ruin and an object of horror, from the wilderness of Diblath throughout all their dwelling places. They will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
But you, son of man, say: This is what the Lord of lords says: The end has reached the land of Israel; the end has reached the four corners of the land.
Now the end is upon you. I will pour out my anger upon you, judge you according to your ways, and bring all your uncleanness upon you.
My eye will not pity you, and I will show no mercy, because I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will remain within you. You will know that I am the Lord.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, disaster is coming after disaster.
The end has come and has hemmed you in.
Dawn has come upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has arrived, and the day of turmoil is near.
Now, very soon, I will pour out my fury on you and pour out my wrath on you. I will judge you according to your ways and bring all your uncleanness upon you.
My eye will not pity, and I will show no mercy. Instead, I will repay you according to your ways, and your uncleanness will remain within you. You will know that I am the Lord who strikes you.
Look, the day has come! Dawn has broken, the rod has budded, and disgrace has blossomed.
Injustice has risen against the rod of the unjust man—not from them, nor from their turmoil, nor from their activity; and he has found no rest among them.
The time has arrived, and the day is near. Let the buyer not rejoice, and let the seller not grieve, because wrath is upon all their possessions.

The buyer will not return to the seller, and there is no longer any life in their lives, because the vision concerning all their possessions will not be reversed. No one will preserve his life through his wrongdoing.
They have sounded the horn and prepared everything, but no one goes to battle, because my wrath is upon all their possessions.
The sword is in the streets, and plague and famine are in the house. Whoever is in the open country will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.
Those among them who escape will escape into the mountains, like doves [?]. They will all die, each for his own sins.
All hands will hang limp, and all knees will run with water.
They will wrap themselves in sackcloth, and shudders will cover them. Shame will be on every face, and every head will be bald.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be despised. Their silver and gold will not be able to rescue them on the day of the Lord’s wrath. They will not satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs. This torment is repayment for their wrongdoing.
As for the glory of their ornaments, which in their pride they made into images of their abominations and their idols, I have therefore made it something despised.
I will hand it over to foreigners as plunder and to the sinners of the land as spoil, and they will defile it.
I will turn my face away from them, and they will defile my sanctuaries. Robbers will enter it and defile it.
They will pass through in chains [?], because the land is full of bloodshed demanding judgment, and the city is full of injustice.
I will bring the shepherds of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses. I will overturn the pride of the mighty, and they will take possession of their sanctuary.
Wrath is coming. They will seek peace, but it will not be found.
Disaster upon disaster will come, and report upon report will be heard. They will seek a vision from the prophets, but instruction will disappear from the priests, and counsel from the elders.

The king will sit in mourning, the ruler will clothe himself in misery, and the hands of the people of the land will hang limp. I will deal with them according to their ways, and judge them by their own judgments. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me. There the hand of the Lord of lords fell upon me.

I looked, and there was a figure with the appearance of fire. From what appeared to be his waist downward there was fire, and from his waist upward I saw something like radiance and like the appearance of God.

He stretched out what looked like a hand and took hold of me by the locks of my hair. The Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in a vision of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the corner gate facing north, where the statue that arouses jealousy stood.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the plain.
He said to me, “Son of man, raise your eyes toward the north.” I raised my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the eastern gate, stood the statue that arouses jealousy, at its entrance.

He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing, having gone far from my sanctuary? Turn again, and you will see the great abominations they are committing.”
He brought me through the gate of the courtyard, and I saw a hole in the wall.
He said to me, “Son of man, dig into the wall.” I dug into the wall and found a doorway.
He said to me, “Go in and see the abominations and evil things they are doing here.”
I went in and saw every kind of image of crawling creatures, animals, and abominable things, and all the idols of the house of Israel, depicted all around the wall.

There were seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. They were standing before him, each with his censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense smoke was rising.

He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness, each in his secret chamber? They say, ‘The Lord does not see us, because the Lord has abandoned the land.’”
He said to me, “Turn again, and you will see the great abominations they are committing.”
He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the Lord’s house on the north side. There I saw women sitting and weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, “Do you see, son of man? Turn again, and you will see abominations greater than these.”

He brought me into the inner courtyard of the Lord’s house. At the entrance to the Lord’s temple, between the portico and the altar, I saw about twenty-five men standing with their backs toward the Lord’s temple and their faces toward the east. They were turning eastward and bowing down to the sun.

He said to me, “Do you see, son of man? Is this abomination they are committing here a small thing to the house of Judah? They have filled the land with injustice and have again provoked me to anger. They are snorting through their nostrils.
“I too will act in fury. My eye will not spare them, and I will have no mercy. They will cry into my ears with a loud voice, but I will not listen to them.”
He called out in my hearing with a loud voice and said, “Come forward, you who are to punish the city, each with his weapons of punishment in his hand.”

I saw six men coming from the direction of the upper gate that faces north, each with his weapons of punishment in his hand. Among them was one man dressed in linen, with a sapphire belt around his waist. They came and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel rose from the cherub that stood over the corner of the temple. He called to the man dressed in linen, with a sapphire belt fastened around his waist.
The Lord said to him, “Go through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations and evil deeds committed within it.”
To those who were with him he said in my hearing, “Go through the city after me and destroy. Let your eyes show no pity, and have no mercy.”

“Kill old men, young men, young women, children, and women, utterly destroying them. But do not approach anyone who bears the mark. Begin at my sanctuary.” So they began with the old men who stood in front of the temple.
He said to them, “Defile the temple and fill the courtyards with the slain. Go out and kill in the city.”
While they were destroying them, I was left alone. I fell facedown and wailed loudly, saying, “Ah, Lord of lords! Are you destroying everyone left of Israel and pouring out your wrath on Jerusalem?”

He said to me, “The wrongdoing of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is filled with blood, and the city is filled with deceit. They say, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land, and the Lord does not see us.’”
“I too will show them no pity and have no mercy. I will repay them for their conduct upon their own heads.”
I saw the man dressed in linen answer and say, “I have done as you commanded me.”
I saw the canopy above the heads of the cherubim, like the appearance of sapphire stone, and something resembling a throne above them.

He called to the man dressed in linen and said to him, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim. Fill your cupped hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.” And he went in before my eyes.
The cherubim were standing on the right side of the temple when that man went in, and the inner courtyard was filled with a cloud.
The glory of God rose from the cherub above the corner of the temple. The temple was filled with a cloud, and the inner courtyard was filled with the radiance of the Lord’s glory.
The sound of the cherubim’s wings could be heard as far as the outer courtyard, like the voice of God when he speaks.
When he commanded the man dressed in linen, he said to him, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim.” He came and stood beside the wheels.
The cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim toward the fire among the cherubim. He took some and placed it in the cupped hands of the man dressed in linen, who took it and went out.
I saw that the cherubim had something resembling a human hand beneath their wings.
I saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. The wheels looked like a stone of Tarshish.
All four had the same appearance and form, like a wheel within a wheel.
When they moved, they went in any of their four directions without turning. Wherever their head went, they followed it without turning.
The entire bodies, backs, hands, and wings of the wheels were full of eyes as they turned to their sides.
He called the wheels “whirling wheels” in my presence.
Each of them had four faces: one was the face of a cherub, another the face of a human, another the face of a lion, and another the face of an eagle.
The cherubim rose up. This was the living creature that I had seen at the River Chebar.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. When the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the earth, the wheels did not turn away from them.
When they stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose, the wheels rose. When the cherubim lifted their wings, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of life was in them.
The glory of the Lord went out from the corner of the temple and stood over the cherubim.

The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before my eyes. As they went out, the wheels went with them. They stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the Lord’s temple, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the River Chebar, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each of them had four faces, and each had four wings, with something resembling a human hand beneath their wings.
Their faces resembled the faces I had seen by the River Chebar, and their appearance was the same. Each went in its own direction.

The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of the Lord’s temple, which faces east. At the entrance of the gate I saw twenty-five men, and among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who plot evil and give wicked advice in this city.
They say, ‘Houses are not being built within it. It is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.’
Therefore prophesy against them. Prophesy, son of man.”
The Spirit of the Lord fell upon me and said to me, “Say: This is what the Lord says: This is what you have loved, people of Israel, and I know the thoughts of your spirit.
You have multiplied those you have killed in this city and filled its streets with ruins.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: “Your slain whom you have cast within it are the meat, and it is the cooking pot. But I will bring you out of it.”
You have feared the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, says the Lord of lords.
I will bring you out of it, hand you over to foreigners, and carry out judgments against you.
You will fall by the sword. At the border of Israel I will judge you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
It will not be a cooking pot for you, nor will you be meat within it. At the border of Israel I will judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. You have not followed my commandments or carried out my judgments, but have acted according to the customs of the nations around you.”
As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fell facedown and cried out loudly, saying, “Ah, Lord of lords! Are you making an end of the remnant of Israel?”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the people of your captivity, and the whole house of Israel will perish—those to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said, ‘Stay far away from the Lord, for the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: I will drive them away among the nations and scatter them among the lands, and I will be a small sanctuary for them in the lands to which they have gone.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: I will gather you from the nations and bring you back from the lands where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
They will enter it and remove all its objects of worship and all its defilements from it.
I will give them a new heart and put a new spirit within them. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh.
They will follow my commandments, keep my judgments, and carry them out. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
For their hearts followed the purpose of their idols and their defilements. I will bring their conduct back upon their own heads, says the Lord of lords.”
The cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
The glory of the Lord rose from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain east of the city.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the land of the Chaldeans, to the exiles, in a vision and by the Spirit of God. Then the vision I had seen departed from me.
And I told the exiles all the words of the Lord that he had shown me.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, you live among a rebellious household. They have eyes but do not see, and ears but do not hear, because they are a rebellious household.
But you, son of man, prepare your belongings for exile, and go into exile by day before their eyes, from your place to another place, so that they may see, because they are a rebellious household.
Bring out your belongings by day before their eyes, like belongings prepared for exile. Then you yourself must go out in the evening, as someone going into exile.
Break through the wall before their eyes and go out through it.
Lift a load onto your shoulder and go out in the darkness. Cover your face so that you cannot see the ground, because I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.

I did as he commanded me. I brought out my belongings by day, like belongings prepared for exile. In the evening I broke through the wall, and in the darkness I went out, carrying the load on my shoulder before their eyes.
In the morning the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, if the house of Israel, that rebellious household, says to you, ‘What are you doing?’
Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: The ruler in Jerusalem will carry this load, and all the house of Israel with him.’
And say to them, ‘I am your sign. Just as I have done, so it will be done to you, and you will go into exile.’
The ruler among you will carry a load on his shoulder and go out in the darkness. He will break through the wall and go out through it. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the ground.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in it. I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, but he will not see it, and there he will die.
I will scatter to every wind all those around him who help him and strengthen him, and I will send the sword after them.
They will know that I am the Lord, who scattered them among the nations and dispersed them through the lands.
I will spare a few of them from the sword, famine, and plague, so that they may recount all their filthy deeds among the nations to which they go. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, you shall eat your bread with trembling and drink your water with trembling and fear.

Say to the people of the land, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the land of Israel: They will eat their bread in fear and drink their water in dismay, because the land and everything in it will be devastated because of the wrongdoing of all its inhabitants.’
The inhabited cities will be devastated, and the land will become a wasteland. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, what is this proverb that people use about you in the land of Israel, saying, “The days drag on, and every vision comes to nothing”?

Therefore, tell them, “This is what the Lord of lords says: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will no longer use it in Israel.” Instead, tell them, “The days are approaching, and every vision will come true.”
There will no longer be any false vision or ambiguous divination among the children of Israel.
For I am the Lord. I have spoken, and I speak a word and carry it out without delay. In your own days, rebellious household, I will speak a word and carry it out, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, look, the house of Israel is saying, ‘The vision this man sees concerns many days from now, and he prophesies about distant times.’
Therefore say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: There will no longer be any delay in my words. Whatever word I speak, I will carry out, says the Lord of lords.’
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy for themselves. Say to those who prophesy out of their own hearts, “Hear the word of the Lord of lords.”
This is what the Lord of lords says: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen no vision!
Your prophets, Israel, have become like foxes among ruins.
You have not gone up into the breach, nor have you built a wall around the house of Israel so that it could stand in battle on the day of the Lord.
They say, “This is what the Lord says,” although the Lord has not sent them, and they have begun to establish a lying word.
You have seen an empty vision and spoken a lying divination. You say, “The Lord has spoken,” but I have not spoken.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have seen empty visions and spoken lies, I am against you, declares the Lord of lords.

My hand will be against the prophets who see empty visions and practice lying divination. They will not be among my people or be recorded in the register of the house of Israel, and they will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord of lords.
Because they have misled my people and said, “Peace,” when there is no peace, and someone was building a wall, and they were plastering it, but it will fall.
Tell those who plaster it that it will fall. Look, I am sending a sweeping rain, and hailstones will fall, and a storm wind.
The wall will break open and fall, and you will be asked, “Where is the plaster you put on it?”
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: “I will make a storm wind blow in my fury. There will be a sweeping rain in my wrath, and hailstones will bring destruction in my fury.”

I will overthrow the wall you plastered, and it will fall. I will throw it to the ground, and its foundations will be exposed. You will fall and perish within it. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
I will spend my anger on the wall and on those who plastered it when it falls. You will be asked, “Where is the wall, and where are those who plastered it?”
These are the prophets of Israel who prophesy about Jerusalem and see visions of peace for her when there is no peace, declares the Lord of lords.
And you, son of man, turn your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own hearts. Prophesy against them and tell them:

This is what the Lord of lords says: Woe to the women who sew cushions for the joints of the arms and make coverings for every head and every height, to hunt down lives! You hunt down the lives of my people while keeping your own lives safe.

You have profaned me before my people for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread, killing people who did not deserve to die and keeping people alive who did not deserve to live, as you lied to a people who listen to lies.

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: I am against your cushions with which you hunt down lives. I will tear them from your arms and release the lives you are hunting, and I will let them fly free.
I will tear your garments and rescue my people from your hands. They will no longer be delivered into the snare in your hands. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

Because you have wounded the heart of the righteous with lies, although I had not caused him pain, and you have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that they do not turn from their evil ways and live,
from now on you will no longer see empty visions or practice divination. I will rescue my people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Some men from among the elders of Israel came to me to inquire of the Lord, and they sat before me.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts and set the stumbling block of their wrongdoing before their faces. I will exact retribution from them.

Now speak with them and tell them: This is what the Lord of lords says: Any man of the house of Israel who raises his idol in his heart, sets the stumbling block of his wrongdoing before his face, and comes to a prophet—I, the Lord, will be a witness against him concerning these things, concerning the multitude of his idols.
This is so that I may seize the house of Israel by their hearts, for they have turned away from me through all their idols.
Now tell the house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: Repent and turn away from all your idols, and turn your faces away from all your defilement.

For any man of Israel, or of those who turn to me and live in Israel, who turns away from me, raises his idol in his heart, sets the stumbling block of his wrongdoing before his face, and comes to a prophet to inquire of him—I, the Lord, will be a witness against him.
I will direct my anger against that man and make him a sign and a proverb. I will destroy him from among my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
If a prophet is led astray and speaks a word, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. I will raise my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
They will bear their guilt. The guilt of the one who inquires will be like the guilt of the prophet.
The house of Israel will no longer stray from me or defile themselves with any of their wrongdoing. Instead, they will be my people, and I will be their God, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, if a land sins against me and commits wrongdoing before me, I will raise my hand against it, break its supply of grain, send famine upon it, and destroy both people and livestock from it.
Even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, they would save only themselves by their righteousness, says the Lord of lords.
If I bring wild beasts upon the land, and they destroy it, leaving it desolate so that no one passes through because of the beasts,
even if these three men were in it, as I live, says the Lord of lords, they would save neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would become desolate.
If I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and destroy both people and livestock from it,
even if these three men were in it, as I live, says the Lord of lords, they would save neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be saved.
If I send a plague upon that land and pour out my fury upon it in bloodshed, destroying both people and livestock from it,
even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live, says the Lord of lords, they would save neither son nor daughter. They would save only themselves by their righteousness.
For this is what the Lord of lords says: I have sent four terrible judgments upon Jerusalem—sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague—to destroy both people and livestock from it.

Yet survivors will remain in it, bringing out sons and daughters. They will come out to you, and you will see their ways and their deeds. Then you will be comforted concerning the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem and everything I have brought upon it.
They will comfort you when you see their ways and their deeds, and you will know that I did not do everything I did to it without cause, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, how does the wood of a vine compare with any other wood—a branch among the trees of the forest?
Is wood taken from it to make anything? Or do people take a peg from it to hang utensils on?
Instead, it is given to the fire as fuel. The fire consumes its two branches, and its middle is charred. Can it be used to make anything?
Even when it was intact, it could not be used to make anything. Now that the fire has consumed it and it is charred, how can it be used to make anything?
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Just as I have given the wood of the vine, out of all the trees of the forest, to the fire as fuel, so I have given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will direct my anger against them. They have escaped from the fire, but fire will consume them. You will know that I am the Lord when I direct my anger against them.
I will make the land a desolation and a horror because they have committed wrongdoing, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, make Jerusalem aware of her defilement.
Say: This is what the Lord of lords says to Jerusalem: Your ancestry and your birth were from the land of Canaan. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
On the day your midwife delivered you, she did not cut your umbilical cord, bathe you in water, rub you with salt, or wrap you in swaddling cloths.
Her eye had no pity on you, to do any of these things for you or show you compassion. Instead, you were thrown out into the open country because your life was despised on the day she delivered you.
I passed by you and saw you writhing in your blood. I said to you, ‘Live in your blood!’
Grow abundantly like the vegetation of the field. You grew and became big and reached [?]. Your breasts developed and your hair grew, but you were naked and bare.

I passed by you and saw you, and I saw that your time had come, the time of maturity. I stretched out my hand over you and covered your nakedness. I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, says the Lord of lords, and you became mine.
I bathed you in water, washed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you in embroidered fabric and put sandals on your feet. I wrapped fine linen around your waist and covered you with silk.
I adorned you with ornaments, put bracelets on your wrists, and a necklace around your neck.
And a beryl between your eyes, earrings in your ears, and a glorious crown on your head.

You adorned yourself with gold and pearls, and dressed in fine linen, blue cloth, and embroidered fabric. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became exceedingly beautiful and attained royal status.
Your beauty became famous among the nations because of the crown of my glory that I placed upon you, says the Lord of lords.
You trusted in your beauty and became a prostitute because of your fame. You poured out your prostitution on everyone who passed by.
You took some of my clothes and made yourself [?], and practiced prostitution in them. They shall not enter, nor shall they be yours.
You took your splendid ornaments, made of the gold and silver I had given you, and made yourself male images, and practiced prostitution with them.
You took your ornamental garments and covered them, and you placed my oil and my incense before them.
The bread I gave you—fine flour, honey, and oil for food—you set before them as a pleasing fragrance, says the Lord of lords.
You took your sons and daughters whom you had borne to me and sacrificed them to them as food, in addition to your prostitution.
You slaughtered my sons and gave them to them as you behaved wantonly with them.
In all your uncleanness and prostitution, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, writhing in blood.
And after all these evil deeds of yours—woe to you, woe to you, says the Lord of lords—
you built yourself a house with vaulted chambers and made yourself high places in every street.
At every crossroads you built your shrines, defiled your beauty, spread your legs for everyone who passed by, and multiplied your acts of prostitution.
You practiced prostitution with the Egyptians, your neighbors with large members. You multiplied your acts of prostitution and provoked me to anger.
I raised my hand against you, took away your allotted provisions, and handed you over to those who hated you, the Philistine women, who rebuked you for your ways of prostitution.
You practiced prostitution with the Assyrians and were not satisfied.
You extended your prostitution to the land of Canaan and of the Chaldeans, and even with these you were not satisfied.
What judgment shall I pass on your daughter, says the Lord of lords, since you have done all these deeds of a shameless prostitute?
When you built your vaulted chambers at every crossroads and your high places in every street, you were not even like a prostitute who collects payment.
Nor were you even like an adulterous married woman who receives from strangers.
People give payment to all prostitutes, but you gave payment to all your lovers. You bribed them in your prostitution to come to you from all around you.
You were different from other women in your prostitution, because you gave payment, while no payment was given to you.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the Lord.

This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you spent your money and exposed your nakedness in your prostitution with your lovers and with all your filthy idols, and gave them the blood of your children,

therefore, I am gathering all your lovers in whom you delighted, everyone you loved, together with everyone you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose your nakedness before their eyes, and they will see all your nakedness.
I will judge you as adulteresses and women who shed blood are judged, and I will hand you over to bloodshed, wrath, and jealousy.
I will hand you over to them. They will demolish your brothels and tear down your shrines. They will strip off your clothes, take your beautiful ornaments, and leave you naked.
They will bring crowds against you, stone you, and strike you with their swords.
They will burn you in the fire and carry out judgments against you before the eyes of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will no longer pay anyone.
I will let my wrath against you subside, and my jealousy will leave you. I will be at rest and will no longer be angry.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth but provoked me with all these things, I too am bringing your conduct back upon your own head, says the Lord of lords, because you practiced uncleanness and prostitution.
Everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: ‘Like mother, like daughter.’

You are the daughter of your mother, who abandoned her husband and her children. You are the sister of your sisters, who abandoned their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives with her daughters on your left. Your younger sister, who lives on your right, is Sodom with her daughters.
You did not merely follow their ways or practice their uncleanness. In a short time you became more corrupt than they were in all your ways.
As I live, says the Lord of lords, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done what you and your daughters have done.
This was the wrongdoing of your sister Sodom: she was proud, had plenty of bread, and lived at ease, she and her daughters, but they did not lend a hand to the needy and the poor.
Instead, they became arrogant and did evil before me. When I saw these things in them, I overthrew them.
Samaria did not commit half as many sins as you did. Your uncleanness exceeded theirs, and through all the uncleanness you practiced, you made your sisters appear innocent.

You too must bear your shame, because through your sins you made your sisters appear innocent. You became more defiled than they were, and they proved more righteous than you. You too must be ashamed and bear your disgrace, because your sisters proved more righteous than you.
I will bring back their captives—the captives of Sodom and her daughters, and the captives of Samaria and her daughters—and I will take your captives captive among them.
So that you may bear disgrace and be ashamed of everything you have done to provoke me to anger.
Your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they were before. Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were before. You and your daughters will also be as you were before.
You did not speak well of your sister Sodom in the day of your pride,
before your wickedness was exposed, as with the reproach of the daughters of Edom and all the daughters of the Philistines who surrounded her and despised her.
You yourself have borne your sins and your uncleanness, says the Lord of lords.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: I will deal with you according to what you have done, because you despised my oaths and broke my covenant.
But I will remember my covenant with you from the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
You will remember your ways and be ashamed when I take your sisters, the older and the younger, and give them to you as daughters, though not through your covenant.
I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Then you will remember and be ashamed, and because of your shame you will never open your mouth again, when I forgive you for everything you have done, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable about the house of Israel.
Say: This is what the Lord of lords says: A great eagle, with large wings, long pinions, full talons, and thick plumage, came to Lebanon and took the topmost shoot of a cedar.
It broke off the top of its growth, brought it to the land of Canaan, and placed it in a city of merchants.
It took some of the seed of the land and set a plant in the open country beside abundant water, and placed it under watch.
It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, so that its shoots faced toward the eagle and its roots were beneath it. It became a vine, produced shoots, and spread out its tendrils.

Then there was another great eagle, with large wings and many talons. This vine turned its roots toward it and extended its branches toward it, so that it would water the vine from the bed where it was planted.
It was planted in a good field beside abundant water, to produce leaves, bear fruit, and become a splendid vine.

Say, “This is what the Lord of lords says: It will not thrive. Instead, its roots will be cut off, and its fruit will decay and wither. All the leaves of its growth will wither. It will not take a mighty arm or a great multitude to uproot it by its roots.”
Look, it is planted, but it will not thrive. When the hot wind blows on it, it will wither in the bed where it sprouted.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Say to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them: Look, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and its officials, and carried them away to Babylon.
He took someone from the royal family, established a covenant with him, and entered into oaths with him. He took away the rulers of the land so that they would not exalt themselves.
Instead, their kingdom was to remain lowly, and they were to keep his covenant and stand by him.
But he will rebel against him and send his messengers to Egypt, so that they may give him horses and a large army. Someone who acts this way will not succeed or escape.
As I live, says the Lord of lords, in the place where they made him king, he who despised my oaths and broke my covenant will die—in the midst of Babylon.
Pharaoh will not wage war with him with a great army or with many horses. Instead, with ambushes and siege towers, he will destroy many lives.
Because he despised the oaths and broke the covenant, he will surrender, and he will not escape, because he has done all these things.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: As I live, because he despised my oaths and broke my covenant, I will bring it down on his head.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in it. I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, and judge him there for the wrong he committed against me.
All his nobles and all his relatives will fall by the sword, and those who remain will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken.
This is what the Lord of lords says: I will take from the topmost shoots of a tall cedar. From its top I will break off its central shoot and plant it on high and lofty mountains.
I will plant it on the mountains of Israel. It will put out leaves, produce fruit, and become a splendid cedar. Every winged bird will dwell in it; they will dwell in the shade of its branches.

All the trees of the open country will know that I, the Lord, have brought down the tall tree and raised up the low tree, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree sprout. I, the Lord, have spoken and have done it.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man,
Why do you repeat this proverb in the land of Israel, saying, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge’?
As I live, says the Lord of lords, this proverb will no longer be repeated in Israel.
For all lives belong to me. The father's life and the son's life belong to me. The person who sins will die.
If a man is righteous and does what is just and right,

and does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes to the idols and objects of worship of the Israelites, does not defile his neighbor's wife, and does not approach a woman during her menstrual period,
does not oppress anyone or defraud anyone, returns the pledge he has taken, gives his bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked with a garment,
does not lend at interest or lend for profit, keeps his hand from wrongdoing, and judges fairly between one person and another,
follows my commandments, keeps my judgments, and acts truthfully—anyone who does this is righteous and will surely live, says the Lord of lords.
But if he fathers a wicked son who sheds blood and does any of these things,
eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbor's wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, defrauds his neighbor, does not return a pledge to its owner, lifts his eyes to idols, and practices impurity,
lends at interest and takes a profit, will he live? He will not live, because he has done all these evil things. He will surely die, and his blood will be on him.
But if he fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has committed and does not do the same,
does not eat on the mountains, does not lift his eyes to the idols of the Israelites, and does not defile his neighbor's wife,
does not oppress anyone, does not take anyone's pledge, does not commit fraud, gives his bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked,

does not turn his hand away from the poor, does not take interest or accept extra payment, carries out my judgments, and follows my commandments, he will not die for his father's wrongdoing but will surely live.
But his father, because he practiced oppression, defrauded his brother, and did not do what was good among his people, will die in his sins.
If they say, “Why is the son not punished for his father's sins?” tell them, “Because the son has done what is just and right and has kept all my commandments, he will surely live.”

The person who sins will die. A son will not be punished for his father's sins, nor will a father be punished for his son's sins. The righteousness of the righteous person will be his own, and the sin of the sinner will be his own.
But if a wicked person turns away from all the sins he has committed, keeps my commandments, and does what is just and right, he will surely live and will not die.
None of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. Instead, he will live because of the righteousness he has practiced.
I do not desire the death of the sinner, says the Lord of lords, but that he turn from his evil way and live.

But if a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits wrongdoing and impurity like the things the sinner has done, none of the righteousness he has practiced will be remembered in his favor. Instead, he will die because of the wrongdoing he has committed and the sins he has sinned.
Yet you say, “The Lord's ways are not right.” Listen, then, house of Israel: my ways are right; it is your ways that are not right.
If a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits wrongdoing, he will die because of that wrongdoing he has committed.
But if a wicked person turns away from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
But if he considers and turns away from all the sins he has committed, he will surely live and will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, “The Lord’s ways are not fair.” My own ways are fair, house of Israel; it is your own ways that are not fair.

Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, says the Lord of lords. Repent and turn away from all your wrongdoing, so that your sins will not become a stumbling block for you.
Throw away from yourselves all the wrongdoing you have committed, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Do not die, house of Israel.
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, says the Lord of lords. Instead, repent and live.
But you, son of man, take up a lament over the rulers of Israel.
Say: What was your mother? A lion’s cub, lying among lions; among lions she raised her cubs.
One of her cubs grew up and became a lion. He learned to tear prey apart and devoured human beings.
The nations heard about him, and he was caught in their trap. They brought him with a bridle to the land of Egypt.
When his mother saw that she had grown weak and her hope was lost, she took one of her cubs and made him a lion.
He walked among the lions and became a lion. He learned to tear prey apart and ate human beings.
He went about in his strength and laid cities waste. He devastated the land and everything in it with the sound of his roaring.
The nations gathered against him from the cities around him. They spread their trap over him, and he was caught in it.
They confined him in a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon. He put him in prison, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted beside water. Its fruit and branches flourished because of abundant water.
It had strong branches for rulers’ scepters. They grew tall among its shoots and were visible because of their height and their many boughs.
They were uprooted in fury and thrown to the ground. A scorching wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were torn off and withered, and fire consumed it.
Now it has been planted in the wilderness, in a thirsty and barren land.
Fire came out from its choice branches and consumed its fruit. No strong branch was found in it anymore, nor a scepter for ruling. This is a lament, and it will remain a lament.
In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some men from among the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord and sat before me.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, speak to the elders of the people of Israel and tell them: Thus says the Lord of lords: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, says the Lord of lords, I will not give you an answer.
Judge them, judge them, son of man, and make known to them the defilement of their ancestors.

Tell them: Thus says the Lord of lords: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand in an oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob and revealed myself to them in the land of Egypt. I raised my hand and told them, “I am the Lord your God.”
On that very day I raised my hand in an oath to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands.
I told them, “Each of you must remove his idol from before his eyes. Do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.”

But they provoked me and refused to listen to me. They did not remove the idols from before their eyes or abandon the idols of Egypt. Then I said that I would pour out my fury on them and fully unleash my anger against them in the land of Egypt.
But I held back for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned among the nations in whose sight I had revealed myself to them, to bring them out of the land of Egypt.
I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
I gave them my commandments and made my laws known to them. Whoever follows them will live by them.
I also gave them my Sabbaths to be a sign between me and them, so that they would know that I am the Lord who makes them holy.

The house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not follow my commandments, and they rejected my judgments, by which a person will live if he carries them out. They profaned my Sabbaths, and I said that I would pour out my wrath on them in the wilderness and destroy them.
But I held back for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
I also raised my hand and swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all countries.
For they rejected my laws and thoroughly profaned my Sabbaths, and their hearts went after their idols.
But my eye had pity on them, so that I did not destroy them or wipe them out in the wilderness.
I said to their children in the wilderness, 'Do not follow your ancestors' commandments, do not keep their laws, and do not defile yourselves with their idols.'
I am the Lord your God. Follow my commandments, keep my laws, and carry them out.
Keep my Sabbaths holy, and let them be a sign between me and you, so that you will know that I am the Lord your God.

But the children provoked me. They did not follow my commandments or keep my laws and carry them out—laws by which a person will live if they follow them. They profaned my Sabbaths, and I said that I would pour out my fury and unleash my anger fully upon them in the wilderness.
But I held back for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned among the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
Nevertheless, I raised my hand and swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.
For they did not carry out my laws, rejected my commandments, and profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes went after their ancestors' idols.
I myself gave them commandments that were not good and laws by which they could not live.
I defiled them through their gifts, when they offered their firstborn, so that I would destroy them and they would know that I am the Lord.
Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and tell them, 'This is what the Lord of lords says: In this too your ancestors blasphemed me, through the treachery they committed against me.'

I brought them into the land that I had raised my hand and sworn to give them. They saw every high hill and every shady tree, and there they slaughtered their sacrifices and presented their offerings. There they placed their pleasing aromas and poured out their drink offerings.
I said to them, 'What is this shrine that you go to?' And it has been called 'the shrine' to this day.
Therefore, son of man, say to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord of lords says: Are you defiling yourselves by following your ancestors' ways and straying after their idols?'

You present your gifts, make your children pass through the fire, and defile yourselves with your idols to this day. Yet you want to inquire of me, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord of lords, I will not give you an answer.
What you have in mind will not happen. You say, 'We will be like the nations, like the peoples of the earth, and worship wood and stone.'
As I live, says the Lord of lords, I will rule over you with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and wrath poured out.
I will bring you out from among the nations and gather you from the lands where you have been scattered, with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath.
I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, and there I will judge you face to face.
Just as I judged your ancestors in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will judge you, says the Lord of lords.
I will make you pass under the rod and bring you under the discipline of the covenant.

I will separate out from among you those who rebel and act unfaithfully against me. I will bring them out of the land where they live, but they will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

But as for you, house of Israel, this is what the Lord of lords says: If you will not listen to me, go and serve your idols, each of you! But no longer defile my holy name with your gifts and your idols.

For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord of lords, there the whole house of Israel will serve me completely. There I will take pleasure in them, and there I will require their first offerings, the first of their crops, and the first of their gifts, with all their holy offerings.

I will accept you as a pleasing fragrance when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you have been scattered. Through you I will show my holiness in the sight of the peoples.
You will know that I am the Lord when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I raised my hand and swore to give to your ancestors.
There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and your faces will cringe at all the evil you have done.
You will know that I am the Lord, who had pity on you for the sake of my name. I have not dealt with you according to your evil ways or your corrupt deeds, house of Israel, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward the south, look southward, and prophesy against the forest in the south.

Say to the forest in the south: Hear the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am setting a fire in you, and it will consume all your trees, both green and dry. Its blazing flame will not be extinguished, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it.
All flesh will see that I, the Lord, have kindled it, and it will not be extinguished.
Then I said, “O Lord of lords, look, they are saying to me, ‘You speak in parables!’”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward Jerusalem, look toward their sanctuary, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you. I will draw my sword from its sheath and destroy both the righteous and the sinner within you.
Because I will destroy both the righteous and the sinner within you, my sword will therefore come out of its sheath against all flesh, from south to north.
All flesh will know that I, the Lord, have drawn my sword from its sheath, and it will not return again.
But you, son of man, groan with your back breaking, and groan bitterly before their eyes.

If they say to you, “Why are you groaning?” tell them, “Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, every hand will hang limp, every spirit will ache, and every knee will run with water. Look, it has come and is happening, says the Lord of lords.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: A sword, a sword has been sharpened!
It has been prepared for slaughter, sharpened to flash like lightning, and prepared to terrify my son's tribe. It has rejected every piece of wood.
He gave it to be prepared and grasped by the hand, for the sword is sharpened and prepared to be handed over to the killers.
Cry out and wail, son of man, because it is coming against my people and against all the leaders of Israel.
Clap your hands, because this has been justified. If the tribe is rejected, it will be no more, says the Lord of lords.

But you, son of man, prophesy and clap your hands together, hand against hand. Let the sword be doubled, even tripled. It is the sword of the slain, the great sword of the slain that makes them tremble.
So that their hearts may break and the wounded multiply at all their gates, I have handed them over to the sword, sharpened, flashing, and prepared for slaughter.
Be strong on my right, and be strong on my left, toward the place where my face is set.
I too will clap my hands together and bring my fury to rest. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
But you, son of man, lay out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to come along. Both must start from the same land. Choose a signpost; choose it at the head of the road to the city.
Make a road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, against Judah, and against fortified Jerusalem.
For the king of Babylon stood at the head of the road, where the roads branch off, to practice divination. He cast an arrow, consulted the idols, and examined his splendor [?].

In his right hand was the divination against Jerusalem: to set ambushes against it, open his mouth with force, raise his voice with a shout, set up mounds opposite its gates, lay ambushes, and build siege towers.
It will seem to them like worthless divination before their eyes, but he will remember wrongdoing and be seized.

Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have remembered your wrongdoing in the captivity of your sins, and have seen your sins and all your practices, you will be seized by the hand.
But you, defiled sinner, ruler of Israel, your day has come—the time of your wrongdoing and your end.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Remove your turban and take off your crown. Raise up the lowly and bring down the exalted.
I will make even this a source of wrongdoing and misery [?], until the one comes to whom judgment belongs, and I will hand it over to him.
But you, son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says concerning the Ammonites and their insults. Say: A sword, a sword prepared for slaughter, sharpened and flashing!
Because of your worthless visions and your false divination, you will be laid upon the necks of wicked sinners whose day has come—the time of their wrongdoing and their end.
Be gathered into your sheath, in the place where you were born, and there I will judge you.
I will pour out my anger upon you and blow upon you with the fire of my fury. I will hand you over to brutal men who bring destruction.
You will be food for the fire, and your blood will be in the midst of the land. You will no longer be remembered, for I, the Lord, have spoken.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
But you, son of man, judge the city of bloodshed and make all its uncleanness known to it.
Say: This is what the Lord of lords says: The city in which blood has been shed—its time has arrived. It has made idols within itself and become defiled.

You have become guilty through the blood you shed, and you have become unclean through the idols you made. Your days have drawn near, and the time of your years has arrived. Therefore I have made you an object of disgrace to the nations and of mockery to all the cities.
Those far from you and those near you will mock you and say, “She whose names are defiled and whose injustices are many!”
Look, the rulers of Israel were within you, each with his clan, to shed blood.
They insulted fathers and mothers within you. They oppressed anyone who turns to me within you, and they mistreated orphans and widows within you.
You despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.
Merchants were within you to shed blood. They ate on the mountains within you and committed sin in your midst.
They uncovered their fathers’ nakedness within you and committed impurity with menstruating women in your midst.
One man defiled his neighbor’s wife, another defiled his daughter-in-law through sexual immorality, and another dishonored his sister, his father’s daughter, within you.

They accepted bribes within you to shed blood. They took interest within you and collected excessive payments within you. They defrauded their friends through oppression, and you forgot me, says the Lord of lords.
I too will strike my hands together because of the wrongdoing you have committed and the blood that has been shed within you.
Will your heart stand firm, and will your hands remain strong in the days when I act? I, the LORD, have spoken and acted.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the countries.
I will take possession of you before the eyes of the nations, and you will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. They are all like bronze, tin, iron, and lead mixed with silver inside a furnace.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have all become mixed together, look, I am gathering you into Jerusalem.
Just as silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead are gathered inside a furnace, and fire is blown upon them to melt them, so I will gather you in my anger and melt you in my wrath.
I will blow the fire of my anger upon you and melt you within it.
As silver is melted inside a furnace, so you will be melted within it. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my fury upon you.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, say to her: You are a land that has not been cleansed or washed, and no rain has fallen upon you.
Her prophets have rebelled within her, like a lion roaring and tearing its prey. They have devoured lives by their violence and taken the valuables from their trade.

Her priests have violated my law and defiled my holy things. They have not distinguished between the holy and the unholy, nor recognized the difference between the unclean and the clean. They have turned their eyes away from my Sabbaths, and I have been profaned among them.
Her leaders within her are like wolves snatching prey, shedding blood and destroying lives to acquire wealth.

Her prophets have plastered her with unsound plaster. They have seen empty visions for them and practiced false divination for them, saying, ‘This is what the LORD says,’ when the LORD has not spoken.
They have oppressed and defrauded the people of the land and mistreated the poor and needy. They have unjustly oppressed anyone who turns to me.
I looked among them for a man who would build a wall and stand in the breach before me on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it, but I found none.
I poured out my anger upon them and consumed them in the fire of my fury. I brought their own ways down upon their heads, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother.
They prostituted themselves in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts were fondled, and there they were deflowered [?].
The older one's name was Oholah, and the other's name was Oholibah. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. Samaria's name was Oholah, and Jerusalem's was Oholibah.
Oholah prostituted herself, turning away from me, and attached herself to her lovers, the Assyrians who were near her.
They were clothed in blue, governors and rulers, desirable soldiers, all of them horsemen riding horses.
She lavished her prostitution on them, on all the choicest Assyrians, and on everyone to whom she attached herself. She defiled herself with their idols.
She did not abandon the prostitution she had practiced in Egypt, for they had dishonored her in her youth. They had deflowered her and lavished their prostitution on her.
Therefore, look, I handed her over to her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians to whom she had attached herself.
They exposed her nakedness and took away her sons and daughters. They killed her with the sword, and she became a subject of talk among women there. They carried out judgments against her.
Her sister Oholibah saw this, but her lust became more corrupt than her sister’s, and her prostitution greater than her sister’s prostitution.
She attached herself to the Assyrians, to the lords and rulers near her, horsemen dressed in blue and riding horses, all of them desirable warriors.
I saw that the way of both of them had become defiled.
She increased her prostitution and saw men portrayed on a wall, images of Chaldeans painted in colors.
They wore belts around their waists and had turbans tied around their heads. They all had the appearance of men, resembling the Babylonians and Chaldeans, the land where they were born.
She attached herself to them as soon as her eyes saw them, and she sent messengers to them in the land of the Chaldeans.
