The Babylonians came to her to sleep with her and defiled her with their prostitution. She became defiled by them, and then she turned away from them in disgust.
She exposed her prostitution and uncovered her nakedness. Then I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.
She increased her prostitution and remembered the days of her youth, when she prostituted herself in the land of Egypt.
She attached herself to their servants, whose genitals were like those of a donkey and whose emissions were like those of horses.
You revisited the wickedness of your youth, when you were deflowered in Egypt and your youthful breasts were fondled.
Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am stirring up against you all your lovers, from whom you turned away in disgust, and I will bring them against you.
The Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Put, Lud, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them will surround you—desirable warriors, lords and rulers, all of them men of Kedar riding horses.

They will come against you armed, with chariots and wagons and crowds of peoples. They will surround you with spears, shields, and helmets. I will place judgment before them, and they will judge you according to their judgments.

I will direct my jealousy against you, and in fury they will smash your nose and tear off your ears. Those remaining among you will fall by the sword. They will carry away your sons and daughters, and what remains of you will be consumed by fire.
They will take your splendid ornaments and strip off your clothes.
I will put an end to your lust and your prostitution brought from the land of Egypt. You will no longer lift your eyes toward them, and you will never remember Egypt again.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am handing you over to those you hated, to the Assyrians, from whom you recoiled.
They will strike you in their hatred and take everything you have worked for. They will leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness of your prostitution and wickedness will be exposed.
These things will be done to you because of your prostitution, because you prostituted yourself by pursuing the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
Because you walked in your sister’s ways, I will put her cup into your hands.
This is what the Lord of lords says: You will drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide, and you will become an object of great and utter ridicule and mockery.
You will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow—a cup of horror and destruction, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it. You will cut off your hair and cut off your breasts, because I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you forgot me and gave yourself over to following your idols, you too must bear your guilt and your prostitution.
The Lord said to me: Mortal, judge Oholah and Oholibah, and show them their defilement.
They committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols, and they burn in the fire their children whom they bore to me.
This is another thing they did to me: they defiled my sanctuary that very day and profaned my Sabbaths.
When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary that very day and profaned it. This is what they did inside my house.
They even sent for men who came to them from far away, men to whom they had sent messengers. When they arrived, they immediately bathed, painted their eyes, and put on their ornaments.
They sat on covered couches, and tables were arranged before them. They took my oil and my incense for themselves.
The sound of their rejoicing went out, along with that of the men who came from Sheba and from the wilderness. They put bracelets on their hands and splendid crowns on their heads.
And I said, “For with these, and with the deeds of prostitutes, they practice prostitution.”
They went in to them as men go in to a prostitute. In this way they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, women who were prostitutes.
Righteous men will judge them with the judgment due to adulteresses and the judgment due to women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.
For this is what the Lord of lords says: Bring an assembly against them and hand them over to terror and plunder.
The assembly will stone them with stones and strike them with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses with fire.
I will put an end to wickedness in the land. All women will be warned and will not practice prostitution as you have.
I will bring your prostitution back upon you, and you will bear the sins of your idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, saying:
Son of man, write down the date of this day, this very day on which the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem.
Tell a parable about the rebellious house and say to them: This is what the Lord of lords says: Set the pot on the fire and pour water into it.
Put into it good, fatty cuts of meat, a shoulder with its bone removed,
from the choicest of the flock. Stoke the bones beneath the pot and burn them underneath it.

For this is what the Lord of lords says: O city of blood, in which the pot is set on the fire, and whose wickedness has not gone out of her! Cut her apart limb by limb, and let no lot be cast over her.
For her blood was within her, and she put it on a rock. She did not pour it onto the ground, so that dust would not cover it.
To stir up wrath for vengeance, I put her blood on a smooth rock so that it would not be covered.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: O city of blood! I myself will make the woodpile large.
Heap up the wood and kindle the fire. Let the meat cook, bring it to a boil, and let the bones burn.
Set it boiling on the coals so that it grows hot and its bronze melts, its uncleanness dissolves within it, and its punishment is completed.
Like diseased figs, the abundance of her wickedness will not go out of her. Rather, her punishment will be by fire.

Because you defiled yourself through prostitution, and because I cleansed you but you were not cleansed of your uncleanness, you will not be cleansed again until I have exhausted my wrath against you.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I am bringing it about, and I will do it. I will not hold back, spare, or show mercy. I will judge you according to your ways and your deeds, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, I am taking away from you the delight of your eyes with a sudden blow. Do not mourn or weep, and do not shed tears.
But groan silently for the dead, and do not hold a mourning ceremony. Fasten your clothes around you, put your sandals on your feet, do not cover your lips, and do not eat the bread of other people.
I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening. The next morning I did as I had been commanded.
The people said to me, “Will you not explain to us what this is that you are doing?”
I said to them, “The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Tell the house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am defiling my sanctuary, the glory of your strength, the delight of their eyes, and what your souls cherish. Your sons and daughters whom you leave behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done. You will not cover your lips, and you will not eat the bread of other people.
Your hair will not be cut, and your sandals will be on your feet. You will neither weep nor dance. You will waste away in your wrongdoing and comfort one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you. You will do just as he has done, and you will know that I am the Lord of lords.
As for you, son of man, on the day when I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the delight of their eyes, what their souls cherish, and their sons and daughters,
on that very day a survivor will come to you and bring the news to your ears.
The survivor will open your mouth on that very day. You will speak and will no longer be silent. You will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

Say to the Ammonites: “Hear the word of the Lord of lords. This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you said, ‘Aha!’ over my sanctuary when it was defiled, over the land of Israel when it was devastated, and over the house of Judah when they went into captivity,
therefore, look, I am giving you to the people of the east as a possession. Their army will settle among you, and they will pitch their tents among you. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a resting place for camels and the land of the Ammonites a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced in your soul over the land of Israel,

therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against you. I will give you as plunder to the nations, wipe you out from among the peoples, destroy you from among the countries, and leave you in ruins. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’
therefore, look, I am laying bare the flank of Moab, stripping it of cities—its cities and their surrounding areas, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
I will give it as a possession to the people of the east and the Ammonites, so that Rabbah of the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
I will execute judgment on Moab, and you will know that I am the Lord.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because Edom took vengeance on the house of Judah, committed a grave offense, and acted against them in jealousy,

Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against Edom. I will destroy its people and livestock and make it a wasteland, from Teman and [?]. It will fall by the sword.
I will carry out my vengeance against Edom through my people Israel. They will take vengeance on Edom according to my anger and my fury, and they will know my vengeance, says the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with the desire of their souls to destroy an everlasting friendship,
therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am raising my hand against the Philistines. I will destroy the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the seacoasts.
I will take great vengeance on them with rebuke and anger. They will know that I am the Lord when I carry out my vengeance against them.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, because Tyre said about Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gates of the peoples have been broken, and they have turned toward me. She is ruined and desolate!’
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Tyre! I will bring many nations against you, as the sea brings up its waves.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and demolish her towers. They will scrape her soil away from her, and I will make her like a smooth rock.
She will become a place for spreading fishing nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords. She will become plunder for the nations.
Her daughter towns in the countryside will be killed by the sword, and they will know that I am the Lord.

For this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am bringing against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, from the north—a king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, an army, and a great multitude.
He will kill your daughter towns in the countryside with the sword. He will erect siege towers against you, set ambushes against you, and erect siege barriers against you.
He will drive the points of his lances into your walls, and they will tear down your towers with their swords.

Sand will cover you from the movement of his horses. Your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and the wheels of his chariots, when he enters your gates like someone entering a city whose walls have been breached.
With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword and throw your towering strongholds down to the ground.
They will plunder your possessions and seize your property. They will demolish your walls and tear down your lovely houses. They will throw your stones, your timber, and your wealth into the sea.
I will put an end to the abundance of your songs, and the sound of your lyre will no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock, a place for spreading fishing nets. You will never be rebuilt, because I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Tyre: The islands will tremble at the sound of your downfall, at the agony of your slain, and at the slaughter taking place within you.

All the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones, take off their robes, and strip off their splendid garments. They will clothe themselves in trembling and sit on the ground. They will tremble without rest and be appalled at you.

They will raise laments over you and say to you, ‘How you have perished, you who inhabited the seas, mighty city, who were powerful on the sea, you and your inhabitants! All your inhabitants have been shattered.’
Now the islands will tremble on the day of your downfall, and the islands will be thrown into turmoil on the day of your downfall.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Tyre: When I make you a ruined city, like cities that are uninhabited, I will bring the deep up over you, and great waters will cover you.

I will bring you down with those who descend into the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the world below, among the ancient ruins, with those who descend into the pit. You will not be inhabited, and I will not establish you in the land of the living.
I will hand you over to destruction. You will be sought, but you will never again be found, says the Lord of lords.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“But you, son of man, raise a lament over Tyre.
Say to Tyre, who sits at the entrance to the sea, the merchant of the peoples and of many islands: This is what the Lord of lords says: Tyre, you said, ‘I am a crown of glory.’
Your borders are in the heart of the seas, and your builders perfected your beauty.
They brought you ribs and planks from Senir, and they took cedars from Lebanon to make masts for you.
They made your oars from the oaks of Bashan, and they made your decking of elephant ivory from the islands of Kittim.
They brought fine linen coverings for your adornment from Egypt to serve as your banner. They brought you blue and purple cloth from the islands of Elishah for your covering.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, were your sailors.
The elders of Gebal and its wise men repaired your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their sailors were among your trading partners.
Persians, Lydians, and men of Put were warriors in your armies. They hung shields and helmets in you, and they were your glory.
The men of Arvad and your armies stood on your walls and guarded your towers. They hung their shields all around your walls and made your beauty complete.
Tarshish was your trading center, with your abundant wealth. They brought you silver, iron, tin, and lead for sale.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants, trading in human beings and bronze vessels.
From Beth-togarmah they brought you horses, horsemen, and mules for sale.
The people of Dedan were your merchants, and many islands were markets for the goods of your hands. They brought you horns of oil and frankincense as gifts.
Edom was your trading center, with the abundance of your products. They brought you purple cloth, fine linen, embroidered cloth, blue cloth, and [?] and [?] for sale.
Judah and the land of Israel were your merchants. They brought you wheat, rice, millet, honey, oil, and resins for sale.
Damascus was your trading center, with the abundance of your products and your abundant wealth, trading in rich wine and white wool.
Dan and Javan from Uzal brought you goods for sale. They brought you iron for you to work, wood, and reeds for sale.
Dedan was your trading center. They brought you an abundance of choice livestock.
They also brought you rams, lambs, and young goats.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah brought you choice spices, precious stones, and gold for sale.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, and Assyria were your trading centers.
These were your merchants, who brought you blue and embroidered garments and fine treasures, secured with ropes, in ships of [?] wood.
The people of Tarshish among your trading partners brought you cargoes, and you became full and very strong.
Your rowers brought you into the heart of the seas and into deep waters. A scorching wind shattered you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth and your earnings from your trading partners, all your warriors, your sailors, and those who repair your leaks from among your trading partners, all your warriors, and the whole assembly within you will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
At the sound of your seafarers’ wailing, those around you will tremble.
All the rowers, the sailors, and all the seafarers will come down from their ships and stand on the land.
They will raise a great and bitter wail over you, throw dust on their heads, and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads for you, wrap themselves in sackcloth, and weep bitterly over you with mourning dances.
Their children will sing laments over you and say, “Who was ever like Tyre, who sat in the midst of the sea?”
When your goods came out of the sea, you satisfied many peoples. With your abundant wealth and trade, you made the kings of the earth rich.
When you were shattered and fell into the depths of the sea, your merchandise and your entire company fell within you.
All the inhabitants of the islands were appalled at you. Their kings trembled, and their faces streamed with tears.
The merchants of the peoples hissed at you. You have come to destruction and will be no more forever.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: This is what the Lord of lords says: Because your heart became proud and you said, ‘I am a god, and I sit on the seat of God in the heart of the seas,’ although you are human and not God, you have considered your heart to be like the heart of God.
Are you perhaps wiser than Daniel, or have you seen hidden things through your wisdom?
With your understanding you have acquired wealth for yourself and gathered silver and gold into your treasuries.
Through your great wisdom and your trade, you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Because you have considered your heart to be like the heart of God,
I am bringing foreigners against you, the mighty ones of the nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and defile your splendor.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of those slain in the heart of the seas.
Will you say before your killers, ‘I am a god’? For in the hands of your killers you are human and not God.
You will die at the hands of uncircumcised foreigners, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre and say to him: This is what the Lord of lords says: You are the seal of likeness, full of wisdom and a crown of glory.

You were in Eden, the garden of God, and were adorned with every precious stone: carnelian, carbuncle, emerald, beryl, sapphire, jasper, crystal, and pearls. You filled your treasuries with gold and your storehouses with precious stones from the day you were created.
You were with the anointed cherub who shelters, and I placed you on the holy mountain of God. You were among the stones of fire.
You walked blamelessly in your ways from the day you were created until wrongdoing was found in you.
Through your abundant trade, you filled your interior with wrongdoing and sinned. I struck you down from the mountain of God, and the sheltering cherub destroyed you from among the stones of fire.
Because your heart became proud of your beauty, your wisdom was corrupted along with your beauty. I threw you to the ground before kings and made you a spectacle for them.

Through the abundance of your [?] and the wrongdoing of your trade, you defiled your sanctuary. I will bring fire out from within you, and it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on the ground in the sight of everyone who sees you.
Everyone among the peoples who knows you will be appalled at you, because you will come to destruction and will be no more forever.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.

Say: This is what the Lord of lords says: I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. They will know that I am the Lord when I carry out my judgments within her and show my holiness in her.
I will send a plague upon her and blood into her streets. Those slain within her will fall by the sword that surrounds her, and they will know that I am the Lord.
No longer will the house of Israel suffer bitter thorns and disfiguring pain from all those around them who treat them with contempt. They will know that I am the Lord of lords.

This is what the Lord of lords says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they were scattered and show my holiness through them in the sight of the peoples, they will live in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live there peacefully, build houses, plant vineyards, and live securely when I execute judgments against all the surrounding nations that oppress them. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Speak and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon lying among the rivers, who says, ‘The river is mine, and I made it.’
I will put a bridle in your jaws and make the fish of your river cling to your scales. I will pull you up out of your river, with all the fish of your river clinging to your scales.

I will throw you into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your river. You will fall on the open ground and will not be gathered up or collected. I have given you as food to the wild animals and the birds of the sky.
All the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you have been like a reed staff to the house of Israel.
When they grasped you with their hands, you pierced their hands. When they leaned on you, you broke and made their loins tremble.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy both people and livestock in you.
The land of Egypt will become a ruin and a wasteland, and they will know that I am the Lord, because you said, “The river is mine, and I made it.”
Therefore, look, I am against you and against your river. I will turn the land of Egypt into devastation and ruin, from Migdol of Syene to the border of Cush.
No human foot will pass through it, nor any hoof of livestock, and it will remain uninhabited for forty years.

I will make the land of Egypt a devastation among desolate cities, and its cities will lie devastated for forty years among ruined cities. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the cities.
This is what the Lord of lords says: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations among whom they were scattered.
I will bring back the captives of Egypt and settle them in the land of Pathros, in the land from which they were sold, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.
It will be the lowliest of all kingdoms and will never again exalt itself above the nations. I will diminish them so that they will not subjugate the nations.
They will no longer be a source of confidence for the house of Israel or a reminder of the wrongdoing of following them. Then they will know that I am the Lord of lords.
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his entire army to hard labor against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder rubbed bare, yet neither he nor his army received any payment from Tyre for the labor he performed against it.

Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take its possessions, carry off its captives, and seize its plunder, and it will be payment for his army.
In return for the work he did against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt, says the Lord of lords.
On that day I will make a horn rise for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Wail and say, ‘Alas for the day!’
For the day is near; the day of the Lord is near—a day of clouds and a time for the nations.
A sword will come against Egypt, and there will be terror in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt, when they take away its wealth and tear up its foundations.
The people of Cush, Put, and Libya, all Arabia, Cub, and the people of the land of the covenant will fall with them by the sword.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Those who support Egypt will fall, and its mighty strength will be broken. From Migdol of Syene they will fall within it by the sword, says the Lord of lords.
They will lie in ruins among ruined lands, and their cities will be among ruined cities.
They will know that I am the Lord when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are shattered.
On that day messengers will go out swiftly from my presence to destroy Cush, which lives undisturbed. Panic will come upon them on Egypt’s day, and look, it is coming!
This is what the Lord of lords says: I am handing over Egypt’s wealth to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
to him and to the mighty men of the nations who are coming to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
I will bring the rivers to ruin and hand the land over to evil men. Through foreigners I will devastate the land and everything in it. I, the Lord, have spoken.
This is what the Lord of lords says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the objects of worship in Memphis. There will no longer be a ruler in the land of Egypt.
I will lay waste the land of Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and carry out judgment on No.
I will pour out my fury on Sin, Egypt’s stronghold, and destroy the wealth of No.
I will set fire to Egypt. Sin will be thrown into turmoil, No will be breached, and Memphis will fall.
The troops of Pi-beseth will become like water. They will fall by the sword and go into captivity.
At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I break Egypt’s scepter there, and the pride of her strength will come to an end. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
I will carry out judgment on Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. It is not being bandaged so that it may heal. No poultice will be put on it, nor will it be bandaged or healed so that it can hold a sword.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt. I will break his strong arms and make the sword fall from his hands.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the countries.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hands. He will cut off Pharaoh’s arms, and Pharaoh will groan before him with the groans of the slain.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall. They will know that I am the Lord when I put my sword in the hands of the king of Babylon and he draws it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the countries. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his forces: Whom do you resemble in your greatness?
Look, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches, dense shade, and a tall trunk. Its top was among the thick branches.
Water made it grow, and the deep made it tall. Its growth spread around the rivers, and it stretched its branches over all the trees of the countryside.
Therefore it grew much taller than all the trees of the countryside. Its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long because of the abundant water that nourished it.
All the birds of the sky nested in its branches. All the wild animals gave birth beneath its boughs, and many nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its greatness and its many branches, because its roots were in abundant water.
The cedars in the garden of God did not surpass it. The fir trees did not resemble its branches, and the plane trees were not like its boughs. No tree in the garden of God resembled it in beauty.
I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees of Eden, the garden of God, envied it.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords says: Because it grew tall, and its top reached among the clouds, and its heart became proud because of its height,
I will hand it over to the mighty ruler of the nations. He will deal with it according to its sin and destroy it.

Foreigners, the mighty among the nations, will destroy it and throw it down on the mountains. Its branches will fall in all the valleys, and its boughs will be broken in all the ravines of the earth. All the peoples of the earth will come out from its shade and abandon it.
When it falls, all the birds of the sky will settle on it, and all the wild animals will be beneath its boughs,

so that none of the trees by the water will grow proud of their height or stretch their tops among the clouds, and none of those that drink water will stand tall or become like them. For they have all been handed over to death, to the earth below, among human beings who go down to the pit.

This is what the Lord of lords says: On the day it went down to Sheol, I brought about mourning. I covered it with the deep and restrained its rivers, and the abundant waters were held back. I made Lebanon mourn over it, and all the trees of the open country withered.

The earth shook at the sound of its fall. When I brought it down to Sheol with those who descend to the pit, all the trees of Eden, the choice and beautiful trees of Lebanon that drink water, were comforted in the earth below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those killed by the sword. Its offspring had lived in its shade among the nations.

Which of the trees of Eden did you resemble in glory and greatness? Yet you have gone down with the trees of Eden to the earth below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his army, says the Lord of lords.
In the eleventh year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: You were like a lion among the nations, but you are like a sea monster in the seas. You thrashed about in your rivers, muddied the water with your feet, and trampled their rivers.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am spreading my net over you through an assembly of many peoples, and they will haul you up in my net.
I will throw you onto the land and cast you down in the open field. I will make all the birds of the sky settle on you and satisfy all the animals of the earth with you.
I will cast your flesh onto the mountains, and the valleys will be filled with your carcasses.
I will drench the land of your watchtowers with your blood, and the mountains and valleys will be filled with you.
When you are extinguished, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. The sun will be covered with clouds, and the moon will not give its light.
I will darken over you all the lights that shine in the heavens, and I will bring darkness upon your land, says the Lord of lords.
I will anger the hearts of many peoples when I bring your destruction among the nations and into lands you do not know.
I will make many nations astonished at you, and their kings will be afraid when I flash my sword before them. They will fear and tremble, each for his own life, on the day of your downfall.
This is what the Lord of lords says: The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
By the sword of warriors I will bring down your strength and that of all the mighty among the nations. They will plunder the strength of Egypt, and all its wealth will be plundered.
I will destroy its livestock beside the abundant waters. Never again will a human foot muddy them, nor will the hoof of an animal.
Then I will make their waters settle and make their rivers flow like oil, says the Lord of lords.
When I make the land of Egypt a wasteland, and the land is devastated with everything in it, when I strike down all its inhabitants, they will know that I am the Lord.
This is a lament, and the daughters of the nations will sing it. They will sing it over Egypt and all its wealth, says the Lord of lords.
In the eleventh year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, raise a lament over Egypt’s army, and bring it down with her among the mighty nations, to the earth below, with those who go down to the pit.
“Go down from pleasant waters and lie down with the uncircumcised.
“They will fall among those killed by the sword, and they will drag him away with his entire army.
“The rulers of the nations will speak with their troops from within Sheol. They will go down and lie there uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword.
“Assyria is there, with its entire company around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword.
“They made its grave in the depths of the pit, and its company was around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, because they caused devastation in the land of the living.

“Elam is there, with its entire army around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the earth below because they caused devastation in the land of the living, and they bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

“Among the slain they made a bed for it, in the midst of its army. Around its grave are all the uncircumcised who were killed by the sword because they caused devastation in the land of the living. They bore their disgrace with those who go down to the pit, and they were counted among the slain.
“Meshech and Tubal are there, with their entire army around their grave, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword because they caused devastation in the land of the living.

“They will not lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were laid beneath their heads. Their guilt rested on their bones because, with their might, they caused devastation in the land of the living.
“But you will lie among the uncircumcised and rest with those killed by the sword.
“Edom is there, with its kings and all its nobles, who, despite their might, were counted among those killed by the sword. They will lie with the uncircumcised and with those who go down to the pit.

“The rulers of the north are there, and all the Sidonians, who went down with those killed by the sword, ashamed and broken despite their might. They lay uncircumcised with those killed by the sword and bore their shame with those who go down to the pit.
“Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over his entire army, killed by the sword—Pharaoh himself and his entire army,” says the Lord of lords.
“For I brought about his destruction in the land of the living, and I laid him among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword—Pharaoh himself and his entire army,” says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land take one man from among them and make him their watchman,
When he sees the sword coming against them, he must blow the horn and warn the people.
“whoever hears the sound of the horn and does not heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
“But if he heeds the warning, he will save his life.

“But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn or warn the people, and the sword comes and takes a life from among them, that person is taken away because of their sins, but I will hold the watchman accountable for their blood.
“But you, son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel, so that you may hear a word from my mouth and warn them on my behalf.

“When I say to the wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ and you do not tell that wicked person to beware of his way, that wicked person will die in his wickedness, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
“But if you warn the wicked person to turn from his way, and he does not turn, he will die in his wickedness, but you will have saved your own life.
“But you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: This is what you have said: ‘Our wickedness and our sins are upon us, and we are wasting away because of them. How can we live?’

“Tell them: As I live, says the Lord of lords, I do not desire the death of the wicked person, but that the wicked person turn from his wickedness and live. Repent and turn away from your evil ways, and do not die, house of Israel.”

But you, son of man, tell your people: The righteousness of a righteous person will not save him on the day he sins, and a wicked person will not stumble because of his wickedness on the day he turns away from it. A righteous person will not live on the day he sins.

When I tell a righteous person that he will surely live, but he trusts in his righteousness and afterward does wrong, none of the righteousness he has practiced will be remembered in his favor. Instead, he will die because of the wrong he has done.
And when I tell a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ but he turns away from his sins and practices justice and righteousness,
If he returns the pledge he took, repays what he stole, follows the commandments of life, and does no wrong, he will surely live and will not die.
none of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. Instead, he will live because of the justice and righteousness he has practiced.
Yet your people say, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ It is their own ways that are not right.
When a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die because of his wrongdoing.
And when a wicked person turns away from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, he will live because of them.
Yet you say, ‘The Lord’s way is not right.’ I will judge each of you according to your ways, house of Israel.
In the eleventh year of our captivity, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and told me, ‘The city has been destroyed.’

Before the escaped man came to me, the Lord’s hand had been upon me in the evening, and he had opened my mouth by the time the escaped man came to me in the morning. Once my mouth was opened, it was no longer shut.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, those living in these ruins in the land of Israel say, “Abraham was only one man, yet he inherited the land. We are many; will we not inherit it?”
Therefore tell them: This is what the Lord of lords says: You eat meat with the blood, you raise your eyes to your idols, and you drink blood. And you want to inherit the land?
You rely on your swords, you practice defilement, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife. And you want to inherit the land?

Tell them: This is what the Lord of lords says: As I live, all who are among the ruins will fall by the sword. All who are in the open country I will give to the wild animals as food, and all who are in holes and caves will die of plague.
I will make the land a place of destruction and horror. The glory of its strength will cease, and the mountains of Israel will become desolate, with no one passing through.
Then they will know that I am the Lord, when I make the land a place of destruction and horror because of all the defilement they have practiced.

As for you, son of man, your people talk about you beside the walls and at the doors of the houses. They speak to one another, each man to his brother, saying, “Come, listen to what word has come from the Lord.”
The people come to you, sit before you, and hear your words, but they do not act on them, because falsehood is in their mouths, and they follow the thoughts of their own hearts.
They regard you as a song, a beautiful voice, and a sweet-sounding harp. They hear your words but do not act on them.
But when your words come to pass, then they will know that you are a prophet among them.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and tell them, the shepherds: This is what the Lord of lords says: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves! Should not the shepherds feed the flock?
You eat the fat animals, clothe yourselves with their wool, and slaughter the fattened animals, but you do not tend the flock.
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bandaged the injured, brought back the straying, or searched for the lost. Instead, you have subjected them to force.
My sheep were scattered because they had no shepherd, and they became food for all the wild animals.
My flock wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My flock was scattered throughout the whole land, with no one to search for them or gather them.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

As I live, says the Lord of lords, because my flock became plunder and food for all the wild animals for lack of a shepherd, and the shepherds did not tend my flock, but instead fed themselves and did not tend my flock—
therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against the shepherds. I will demand my flock from their hands and stop them from tending my flock any longer. I will rescue my flock from their mouths, and they will no longer be food for them.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I myself will seek out my flock and care for them.
As a shepherd cares for his flock on a windy day, so I will care for my flock. I will gather them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.

I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the countries, and bring them into their own land. I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

I will pasture them in a good grazing place, and their dwelling will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in a good dwelling place and graze in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will pasture my flock, and I myself will make them lie down, says the Lord of lords.
I will seek the lost, bring back the straying, bind up the injured, and strengthen the sick. I will watch over the fat and the strong, and I will pasture them with justice.
As for you, my flock, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I will judge between one sheep and another, and between one ram and another.
Is it not enough for you shepherds to graze on good pasture, that you trample the rest of your pasture underfoot? You drink the water, but you muddy what you leave behind with your feet.
My flock grazes on what your feet have trampled and drinks the water your feet have muddied.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the weak sheep.
Because they kept pushing with their sides and shoulders and butting all the sick ones with their horns, until they scattered them outside,
I will rescue my flock, and they will no longer be plunder for them. I will judge between one sheep and another, and between one ram and another.
I will appoint a shepherd over them, and he will tend them: my servant David. He will tend them, and he will be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and my servant David will be ruler among them.
I will establish a covenant of peace for them and rid the land of dangerous animals. They will live peacefully in the wilderness and sleep in the forest.
I will give them my blessing around my hill. I will send down rain in its season, and it will be rain of blessing.

The trees of the land will bear fruit, and the land will yield its crops. They will live securely in their land, and they will know that I am the Lord when I break their yoke and rescue them from the hands of those who enslave them.
They will no longer be plunder for the nations, nor will wild animals devour them. They will live securely, and no one will terrify them.
I will establish a planting of peace for them. They will no longer suffer from famine in the land, and they will no longer endure the scorn of the nations.
They will know that I am the Lord their God and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, says the Lord of lords.
As for you, my flock, the flock of my pasture, you are human beings, and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
Say to it: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Mount Seir. I will raise my hand against you and make you a ruin and a horror.
I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will be devastated. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you harbored perpetual hostility and handed the people of Israel over to the sword at the time of their distress, at the time of the iniquity of their end,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord of lords, I will hand you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. The blood you hated—that blood will pursue you.
I will make Mount Seir a ruin and a horror, and I will destroy from it those who pass through and those who return.
I will fill his mountains with his slain. Those slain by the sword will fall on your cliffs, on your heights, and in your valleys.
I will make you a ruin forever, and your cities will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you said, ‘These two nations and these two kingdoms are mine, and I will possess them,’ even though the Lord was there,
therefore, as I live, says the Lord of lords, I will deal with you according to your anger and the hostility you showed in hating them. I will reveal myself among them when I judge you.
Then you will know that I am the Lord. I have heard all your blasphemy that you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying, ‘They are desolate, and they are ours to devour.’
You opened your mouths wide against me and multiplied your words against me, and I heard.
This is what the Lord of lords says to Mount Seir, which dwells amid the joy of the whole earth: I will make you a wasteland.

Because you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel when it became desolate, I will do the same to you. You will become a wasteland, Mount Seir and all Edom. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy concerning the mountains of Israel, and say to the mountains of Israel: Hear the word of the Lord of lords.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because the enemy said about you, ‘Aha!’ and said, ‘The ancient heights are ours as a possession,’

therefore prophesy and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Because you were dishonored, devastated, and reviled by those around you, and became a possession of the remaining nations, and became the subject of people's talk and the gossip of the nations,

therefore hear the word of the Lord of lords, mountains of Israel. This is what the Lord of lords says to the mountains, the heights, the valleys, the ravines, the deserted ruins, and the abandoned cities that became plunder and an object of mockery for the remaining nations around them:

Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the remaining nations and against all Edom, because they made my land their possession. With joy in their hearts they dishonored people, taking them captive and plundering them.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains, the heights, the valleys, and the ravines: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and my fury because you have borne the disgrace inflicted by the nations.
Therefore, this is what the Lord of lords says: I have raised my hand against the nations around you, so that they will bear their own disgrace.
But you, mountains of Israel, will put forth your branches and produce abundant fruit for my people Israel, for they will soon come.
Look, I am turning toward you, and you will be cultivated and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel. The cities will be inhabited, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

I will multiply people and livestock upon you, and they will increase and become numerous. I will settle you as in former times and do good to you as at the beginning. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
I will cause people, my people Israel, to walk upon you. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will never again be bereaved.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Because they say to you, ‘You devour human beings and bereave her people,’
from now on you will not devour human beings, and you will no longer bereave your people, says the Lord of lords.
I will no longer let the insults of the nations be heard against you. You will no longer bear their contempt, and you will no longer bereave your people, says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their ways and their deeds. Their conduct before me was like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman.
I poured out my anger upon them because of the blood they shed in the land, and because they defiled it with their idols.
I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them among the cities. I judged them according to their ways and their deeds.
They went among the nations and defiled my holy name. The nations said of them, “These are God's people, yet they have left his land.”
I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had defiled among the nations to which they went.

Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord of lords says: It is not for your sake that I am acting, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have defiled among the nations to which you went.

I will make my great name holy, the name that was defiled among the nations, which you defiled among them. The nations will know that I am the LORD, says the Lord of lords, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.
I will bring you out from the nations, gather you from the countries, and bring you to your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you and cleanse you from all your uncleanness and from all your idols.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to follow my commandments and to keep my judgments and carry them out.
You will live in the land that I gave your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you.
I will increase the fruit of the trees and the crops of the land, and you will no longer suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
There you will remember your evil ways and your contemptible deeds, and your faces will cringe because of your wrongdoing and your uncleanness.
Know that it is not for your sake that I am doing these things, says the Lord of lords. Be ashamed and accept correction for your evil ways, so that you do not die, house of Israel.
This is what the Lord of lords says: On the day when I cleanse you from all your wrongdoing, I will make the cities inhabited and rebuild the ruins.
The land that was ruined will be cultivated, though it had lain desolate in the sight of everyone who passed by.
They will say, “That ruined land has become like the garden of Eden, and the cities that were ruined and overthrown have become strong fortified towns.”
The nations remaining around you will know that I, the LORD, rebuild what was overthrown and plant what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Again, in this matter I will seek out the house of Israel to act for them, and I will make them numerous like a flock of people.
Like the consecrated flocks, like the flocks of Jerusalem at the time of her festivals, so will the cities that were ruined be filled with flocks of people. And they will know that I am the LORD.
The hand of the LORD was upon me, and the LORD brought me out by his Spirit and set me down in a valley. It was full of bones.
He led me around among them, and I saw that there were very many in the valley, and they were very dry.
He said to me, “Son of man, can these bones live?” I said, “You know, Lord of lords.”
He said to me, “Prophesy over these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.
This is what the Lord of lords says to these bones: Look, I am bringing breath into you, and you will live.
I will put sinews on you, make flesh grow on you, cover you with skin, and put breath into you. You will live, and you will know that I am the LORD.”
I prophesied as he commanded me, and as I prophesied there was a sound and a shaking, and the bones came together, each bone to its joint.
I saw sinews and flesh grow over them, and skin covered them, but there was no breath in them.

He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: This is what the Lord of lords says: Come, breath, from the four winds, and breathe into these slain people so that they may live.”
I prophesied as he commanded me, and breath entered them. They came to life and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
He said to me, “Son of man, all these bones belong to the people of Israel, who were saying, ‘Our bones have dried up, our hope has perished, and we are finished.’”
Therefore prophesy and say to them, “This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am opening your graves and bringing you up from your graves, and I am bringing you to the land of Israel.”
You will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves and bring you up from your graves.
“I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live. I will settle you in your land, and you will know that I am the Lord. I have spoken, and I will act,” says the Lord of lords.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“But you, son of man, take a stick and write on it, ‘Judah and the people of Israel associated with him.’ Take another stick and write on it, ‘Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the people of Israel associated with him.’
Bring them together, one beside the other, so that they become one stick in your hand.
If your people say to you, ‘Tell us what these things mean,’

say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim’s hand, and the tribes of Israel associated with him. I will put them with the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand.’
Hold the sticks on which you write in your hand before their eyes.
Say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am taking the people of Israel from among the nations to which they have gone. I will gather them and bring them to their land.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule them all. They will no longer be two nations, and they will never again be divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their abominations, or any of their wrongdoing. I will rescue them from all the places where they have lived and sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
My servant David will reign over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my laws, keep my commandments, and carry them out.

They will live in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, where their ancestors lived. They, their children, and their grandchildren will live there forever, and my servant David will be their ruler forever.
I will establish a covenant of peace with them, and it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will increase their numbers and place my sanctuary among them forever.
My dwelling will be among them, and they will be my people.
The nations will know that I am the Lord who makes Israel holy, when my sanctuary is among them forever.’”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Son of man, turn your face toward Gog and toward the land of Magog, the ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him and say,
‘This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Gog, ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal.

I will gather you, put a bridle in your jaws, and bring you out of your land—you and your entire army, horses and horsemen, all wearing armor, a great assembly with spears and shields, wielding swords.
All the Persians, Cushites, and people of Put are with them, with shields and helmets.
Gomer and its entire army, Beth-togarmah and the far reaches of the north and all their armies, and many nations are with you.
Get ready, you and your entire assembly gathered with you, and be their guard.

You were appointed from ancient days, and in the latter years you will come against the mountains of Israel and against a land that has recovered from the sword and has been gathered from many nations. They will all live in it peacefully.
You will advance like a storm and like a cloud covering the land—you and all your army and the many peoples with you.
This is what the Lord of lords says: On that day, thoughts will arise in your heart, and you will devise an evil plan.
You will say, “I will go up against a prosperous land and attack those who live peacefully, who have no walls, bars, or gates.”

You will take captives and seize plunder, and turn your hand against the ruined places that have been resettled and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions and live in the finest part of the land.

Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all the towns will say to you, ‘Have you come to take captives and seize plunder? Have you gathered your forces to carry off silver and gold, take livestock and possessions, and carry away a great haul?’
Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: This is what the Lord of lords says: On the day when my people Israel live in peace, you will know.
You will come from your place in the farthest reaches of the north, with many peoples accompanying you, all riding horses—a great gathering and a vast army.

You will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the last days you will come, and I will bring you against my land, so that the nations may know me when I show my holiness through you before their eyes.

This is what the Lord of lords says: You are the one of whom I spoke in former days through my servants, the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days and in these years that I would bring you against them.
On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, says the Lord of lords, my anger will burn in my fury.
In my zeal, in the fire of my anger, I have declared that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the wild animals, every creature that crawls on the earth, and all human beings on the face of the earth will tremble before it. The mountains will be overturned, the towers will fall, and all the walls will fall to the ground.
I will summon a sword against him throughout all my mountains, says the Lord of lords. Each man's sword will be against his brother.
I will judge him with plague and bloodshed. I will send torrential rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur down upon him, upon his leaders, and upon the many peoples with him.
I will show my greatness and my holiness before the eyes of many nations, and they will know that I am the LORD.
And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what the Lord of lords says: Look, I am against you, Gog, ruler and chief of Meshech and Tubal.
I will subdue you, gather you, bring you up from the far reaches of the north, and bring you to the mountains of Israel.
I will strip your bow from your left hand and your arrow from your right.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you and all your army and the many peoples with you. I will give you as food to the winged birds and the animals of the earth.
You will fall in the open country, for I have spoken, says the Lord of lords.
I will send fire upon Magog and upon the inhabitants of the islands who live peacefully, and they will know that I am the Lord.
I will make my holy name known among my people Israel, and I will no longer profane my holy name. The nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
Look, the day of which I spoke is about to come, says the Lord of lords.
The inhabitants of the towns of Israel will go out and set fire to the weapons, shields, javelins, bows, arrows, hand clubs, and spears. They will burn them as fuel for seven years.

They will not need wood from the fields or the forest, but will burn their weapons in the fire. They will take captive those who took them captive and plunder those who plundered them, says the Lord of lords.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place there in Israel, a great valley east of the sea. They will block the valley and bury Gog and all his army there, and it will be called the Valley of Gog's Destruction.
For seven months the house of Israel will bury them, and the land will be cleansed.
All the people of the land will bury them, and this will bring them renown on the day when I am glorified, says the LORD.
After seven months, men will continually travel through the land and bury those who remain in the land, so that it may be cleansed.
Everyone who passes through the land and sees a human bone will set up a marker beside it, until those who bury the dead in the Valley of Gog come and take it away.
The city will be named “Mighty,” and they will cleanse the land.

But you, son of man, say to every bird of the sky and every wild animal: Thus says the Lord of lords: Gather and come from every place to the great sacrifice that I am preparing for you on the mountains of Israel. You will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of warriors and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth—of rams, fattened animals, goats, bulls, and [?] of Bashan, all of them.
You will eat flesh until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, from the sacrifice that I am preparing for you.
At my table you will be filled with the flesh of horses and their riders, of warriors and all fighting men, says the Lord of lords.
I will establish my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I have carried out and the hand I have laid upon them.
The house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God, from that day onward.

The nations will know that the Israelites went into captivity because of their wrongdoing, because they acted unfaithfully toward me. I turned my face away from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I repaid them according to their uncleanness and their wrongdoing, and I turned my face away from them.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of lords: Now I will bring back the captives of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name.
They will bear all their shame and the wrongdoing they committed against me when they live peacefully in their land, with no one to frighten them,
when I gather them from the nations and bring them back from the cities of their enemies, and through them show myself holy in the sight of many nations.
They will know that I am the Lord their God. I sent them into captivity among the nations, and I will gather them into their own land and leave none of them there.
I will not turn my face away from them, but I will pour out my spirit upon the whole house of Israel, says the Lord of lords.

In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was destroyed, on that very day the hand of the Lord came upon me.
He brought me there in a vision of God. He brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain. On its southern side was something like the structure of a city.
He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. In his hand were a linen cord and a measuring rod, and he was standing in the gateway.

That man said to me, “Son of man, look with your eyes, listen with your ears, and take to heart everything I show you, because you have come here so that I may show it to you. Tell the Israelites everything you see.”
I saw a wall surrounding that building. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six cubits and a handbreadth long. He measured the thickness of the structure: one rod; and its height: one rod.
He came to the gate facing east, went up its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate: one rod wide; and the other threshold: one rod wide.
The vestibule was one rod long and one rod wide. Between the vestibules were five cubits, and the threshold of the gate, inward from the gate's vestibules, was one rod.
He measured the vestibule of the gate: eight cubits. The gate's inner threshold was two cubits.
Inside the eastern gate there were three on this side and three on that side. All three had the same measurements, and the vestibules on either side had the same measurements.
He measured the width of the gate's entrance: ten cubits; and the length of the gate: thirteen cubits.
The barrier in front of the threshold was one cubit on each side, and its interior was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
He measured the gateway from roof to roof: twenty-five cubits wide, with one entrance opposite the other.
He made the space in front of the gateway sixty cubits, and the space in front of the other, outer gateway sixty cubits.
In front of the inner gateway were fifty cubits.
There were windows, wide on the inside and narrow on the outside, in the [?] and in the gateway’s porticoes. They had windows all around on the inside.
He brought me into the outer courtyard, and I saw steps all around: thirty steps, one above another.
The steps beside the gateway were opposite the length of the steps.
He measured its width from in front of the courtyard gateway: one hundred cubits to the east and to the north.
He measured the length and width of the gateway in front of him on the north side of the courtyard.
Its measurement was three on this side and three on that side, like the measurement of the first gateway: fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Its windows and porticoes had the same measurements as the gateway facing east. Seven steps led up to it, and there was a threshold in front of them.
The gateways of the inner courtyard were opposite the gateway to the north and east. He measured one hundred cubits from gateway to gateway.
He led me toward the south, and I saw the southern gateway. He measured its porticoes and its posts according to these measurements.
It and its porticoes had windows all around, like these windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
Seven steps led up to it, and there was a threshold in front of it. It had palm trees on its porticoes, one on this side and one on that side.
The gateways of the inner courtyard were toward the south. He measured one hundred cubits from gateway to gateway.
He brought me into the inner courtyard through the southern gateway and measured the southern gateway according to these measurements.
Its interior, porches, and thresholds had these same measurements, and it and its porches had windows all around. Its length was fifty cubits and its width twenty-five.
Its walls surrounded it; they were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
The porticoes of the outer courtyard had palm trees in them, and they had eight steps.
He brought me into the inner courtyard from the east and measured the gateway according to these measurements.
Its interior, its porticoes, and its thresholds; it and its porticoes had windows all around. The length was fifty cubits and the width twenty-five.
The threshold of the outer courtyard; there were palm trees in the porticoes on either side, and it had eight steps.
He brought me to the northern gateway and measured it according to these measurements.
Its interior, its porticoes, and its thresholds; windows surrounded it. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
The porticoes of the outer courtyard; there were palm trees in the porticoes on either side, and it had eight steps.
There was a hall whose entrance was in the gateway’s portico, and there they placed the whole burnt offerings.
In the porticoes of the gate were two tables on one side and two tables on the other, on which to slaughter whole burnt offerings, offerings, and offerings for purification from sins.
Beside the north gate, outside the area for whole burnt offerings, were two tables, and on the other side of the portico were two tables.
There were four tables on one side and four tables on the other in the porticoes of the gate—eight tables on which they slaughtered the animals.

There were four tables of cut stone for the whole burnt offerings, each a cubit and a half long and a cubit and a half wide. On them they placed the tools with which they slaughtered the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
Their rims were a handbreadth wide all around, and on the tables they placed the meat of the offerings.
Outside the inner gate were the officials’ rooms, in the inner courtyard beside the north gate, facing south. One was beside the east gate, facing north.
He said to me, “This chamber facing south is for the priests who carry out the duties of the temple.

The chamber facing north is for the priests, the descendants of Zadok, who carry out the duties of the altar. They are the ones among the descendants of Levi who approach to perform the service of the Lord.”
He measured the courtyard: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a square. The altar stood in front of the temple.

He brought me to the threshold of the temple and measured the threshold: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. The width of the gate was three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
The threshold was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide. Steps led up to it, and pillars stood by the porticoes, one on either side.
He brought me into the sanctuary and measured the portico: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other, and the width of the tabernacle.
The gate was ten cubits wide, and the sides of the gate were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. He measured its length at forty cubits and its width at twenty cubits.
He went inside and measured the doorway: two cubits; the gate: six cubits; and its width: seven cubits.
He measured its length at twenty cubits and its width at twenty cubits, facing the sanctuary. He said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
He measured the wall of the temple: six cubits. The side chamber was seven cubits wide, all around the temple.

The side chambers were arranged chamber above chamber, thirty-three times. The side chambers extended into the wall of the temple all around, so that they would be held in place while remaining separate from the wall.

Those side chambers continued upward, circling around the upper part of the temple so that the temple became wider above. They would go up from below to the middle chambers, and from the middle chambers to the upper ones.
I saw the height of the temple all around. The side chambers were separated from one another by a full reed, six cubits.
The outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits thick, and the inner wall was five cubits thick.
Between the chambers surrounding the house, the width was twenty cubits.
The side chamber had doorways opening onto the space left clear, one toward the south and one toward the north. The space left clear was five cubits wide.
The building in front of the separate area, at the western gate, was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
He measured the temple: a hundred cubits long. The separate area of the walled building was a hundred cubits long.
The width in front of the temple and the eastern separate area was a hundred cubits.

He measured the length of the building in front of the separate area, behind it, together with its galleries on either side: a hundred cubits; also the inner sanctuary and the porticoes of the courtyard gate.
And the thresholds, windows, and panels around all three of their doorways were covered with wood all around, along its length as far as the windows.
The windows were covered above the doors of the inner house and outside. He measured all the walls all around, outside and inside.
He made cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between one cherub and another, and each cherub had two faces.
A human face faced the palm trees on either side. This was done throughout the house, all around.
From the ground to above the doorways, cherubim and palm trees were made.
The wall of the temple was on the west, and the front of the sanctuary had the appearance
of a wooden altar, three cubits high and two cubits long. It had horns, and its length and its panels were of wood. He said to me, “This is the table that stands before the Lord.”
And there were two doors for each folding doorway,
two for one folding doorway and two for the other folding doorway.
On them, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm trees were made, just as they were made on the walls. The front of the porch was covered with wood on the outside.
There were recessed windows and palm trees on either side, along the sides of the porch, and the sides of the house were covered with boards.
He brought me out into the outer courtyard toward the north and brought me into the chamber opposite the separate area and opposite the northern building,
opposite the length of [?] cubits at the northern gate, and fifty cubits wide,
opposite the gate of the inner courtyard and opposite the steps of the outer courtyard, which were built one above another in three tiers.
In front of the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. The entrance to the walkway faced north.
The upper chambers were smaller because the steps extended into them.
For they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courtyard. Therefore they were smaller than the lower and middle chambers.
The outer wall opposite the chambers was fifty cubits long.
For the length of the chambers of the outer courtyard was fifty cubits, while those opposite the temple were a hundred cubits long.
And the doorway of the chamber at the eastern entrance led into the outer courtyard.
Along the width of the courtyard wall, at the eastern entrance, in front of the separate area and in front of the building, were chambers.
There was a path in front of them. They looked like the chambers toward the north, with corresponding length and width, and corresponding exits, entrances, appearance, and doors.
Like the doors of the chambers toward the south, there was a door at the head of the path, the path in front of the wall toward the eastern valley, as one came in.

He said to me, “The northern chambers and the southern chambers in front of the separate area are the chambers where the priests who approach the Lord eat the most holy things. There they place the most holy things, the fine flour, and the offering for purification from sins, because it is a holy place.

When the priests enter, they must not go out from the sanctuary into the outer courtyard. Instead, they must leave there the garments in which they minister, because they are holy, and put on other garments and present offerings on behalf of the people.”
He finished measuring the inner house and brought me out by way of the gate facing east, and he measured it all around.
He measured the eastern side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds.
He measured the north side with the measuring rod: five hundred rods all around.
He measured the south side: five hundred rods with the measuring rod.
He measured the western side: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate the holy from the common.
He brought me to the gate facing east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east. His voice was like the sound of mighty waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
It was like the vision I saw when I came to destroy the city, and like the vision I saw by the River Chebar. I fell facedown.
The glory of the Lord entered the temple through the gate facing east.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard, and I saw that the glory of the Lord filled his temple.
I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, while the man stood beside me.

He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will no longer defile themselves, nor will they and their kings defile my holy name with their prostitution, the corpses of their kings, and their idols.

They placed their gates beside my gates and their thresholds beside my thresholds, with a wall between me and them. They defiled my holy name with the wickedness they committed, and I destroyed them in my anger.
Now let them remove their prostitution and the corpses of their kings from my presence, and I will dwell among them forever.
