But you, son of man, show this temple to the house of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of the wrong they have done against me, and let them measure its design.

If they are ashamed of what they have done, show them the temple’s designs, its arrangement, its entrances and exits, its entire design, all its laws, and all its forms. Draw it before their eyes so that they may observe all its forms and its entire plan and carry them out.
This is the vision of the temple: on the mountaintop, its entire surrounding territory is most holy.

These are the measurements of the altar, using a cubit consisting of a cubit and a handbreadth. Its hollow base was a cubit by a cubit, and it had a rim along its edge, a span all around, and likewise on its outer side.
From the ground to the lower ledge was two cubits, and its width was one cubit. From the lower ledge to the upper one was four cubits, and its width was a cubit.
The altar hearth was four cubits high, and four horns rose above the hearth.
The altar hearth was twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
Its ledge was fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide on its four sides. Its rim and the border around it were half a cubit, and it had a hollow base all around. Its steps faced east.
He said to me, “Son of man, this is what the Lord of lords says: These are the regulations for the altar when it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and sprinkling blood on it.
Give a young bull as an offering for cleansing from sins to the priests and Levites descended from Zadok, who approach me to serve me, says the Lord of lords.
Take some of its blood and sprinkle it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of its ledge, and on the border around it. Sprinkle it, and it will be cleansed.
Take the bull for the cleansing offering, and they shall burn it beside the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day, offer a male goat without blemish as a cleansing offering, and they shall cleanse the altar just as they cleansed it with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, offer a young bull without blemish and a ram from the flock without blemish.
Present them before the Lord, and let the priests throw salt on them and offer them as whole burnt offerings to the Lord.
For seven days you shall offer one male goat each day as a purification offering. They shall also offer one young bull and a ram from the flock without blemish for seven days.
They shall purify the altar and consecrate themselves.
When these days are completed, from the seventh day onward, the priests shall offer their whole burnt offerings and their offerings on the altar, and I will accept them, says the Lord of lords.
He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces east, and I saw that it was shut.
The Lord said to me, “This gate shall remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall enter through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered through it. It shall remain shut.
The ruler shall sit in it and eat bread before the Lord. He shall enter by way of the threshold gate and leave by the same way.”
He brought me in by way of the north gate in front of the temple. I saw that the glory of the Lord had filled the temple, and I fell on my face.

The Lord said to me, “Son of man, pay close attention, look with your eyes, and listen with your ears to everything I tell you, to all the laws of the temple and all its designs. Pay attention to the entrances of the temple and the exits of the sanctuary.
Say to the rebellious house of Israel: Thus says the Lord of lords: Has all your defilement not been enough for you, house of Israel?

You even bring in foreigners who are uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh. They are in my sanctuary and defile my temple, while you offer fat and blood along with my bread. You break my covenant with all your defilement.
You have not kept charge of my sanctuary, but you have appointed your own guards to keep charge of my sanctuary.
Thus says the Lord of lords: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my sanctuary—not even a foreigner who lives among the people of Israel.
Nor shall the Levites who withdrew from me when the people of Israel strayed from me after their idols. They must bear their guilt.
They were in my sanctuary and served at the gate of the temple. They shall slaughter the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices of the people, and they shall stand before them and serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block that led the people of Israel into sin, I have raised my hand against them, says the Lord of lords, and they must bear their guilt.
They shall not approach me to serve me, nor shall they approach any of my holy things in the Most Holy Place. They shall bear all their shame and all the defilement they have committed.
I will make them responsible for the care of the temple and for doing all the work that takes place in it.

But the priests and Levites, the descendants of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel strayed from me, shall approach me to serve me. They shall stand before me and offer me fat and blood, says the Lord of lords.
They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table to serve me and carry out their duties to me.
When they enter the gate of the inner courtyard, they shall wear linen garments. They shall not wear wool while serving at the gate of the inner courtyard or farther inside.
They shall put linen turbans on their heads and tie linen undergarments around their waists.

When they go out to the outer courtyard to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they serve and leave them in the holy chamber. They shall put on other garments so that they do not make the people holy through their garments.
They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but shall keep the hair on their heads trimmed.
The priests must not drink wine when they enter the inner courtyard.
They shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin descended from Israel, or a widow whose deceased husband was a priest.”
They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and make known to them the difference between the unclean and the clean.
They shall stand as judges in disputes and judge according to my judgments. They shall keep my laws and my commandments at all my appointed festivals, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.
They shall not go near a dead person and become unclean. But they may become unclean for a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or virgin sister who has not married.
After he becomes defiled, he must count seven days for himself, and then he will be purified.
On the day he enters the sanctuary, into the inner court to serve in the holy place, he shall present his purification offering, says the Lord of lords.
They shall have an inheritance: I myself am their inheritance. You shall give them no portion in Israel; I myself am their portion.
They shall eat the fine flour and the purification offering for sins, and everything devoted in Israel shall belong to them.
The first of all the firstfruits, from all the contributions you set apart, shall belong to the priests. Give the first of your dough to the priests, so that a blessing may rest upon your houses.
The priests must not eat any bird or animal that has been strangled or torn apart.

When you divide the land, set apart a contribution for the Lord and consecrate a portion of the land. Its length shall be twenty-five thousand and its width ten thousand, and all its boundaries around it shall be holy.
There shall be an area for the sanctuary, five hundred by five hundred, square on all sides, with fifty cubits of open space around it.
From this measured area, the length shall be twenty-five thousand and the width ten thousand, and within it shall be the Most Holy Place.

The holy portion of the land shall belong to the priests who serve in the Lord’s sanctuary and approach to serve the Lord. It shall provide them with a place for houses and a sanctuary for the holy things.
It will be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, and it will be an inheritance for the Levites who serve in the house: twenty houses.
The city’s property shall be five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the allotment for the sanctuary. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
The ruler shall have land alongside the holy allotment and the city’s property, on the east and on the west. Its length shall correspond to that of an allotment, from east to west.
It shall be an inheritance for the people of Israel. The rulers of my people shall no longer oppress them, and they shall give the land to the people of Israel according to their tribes.
This is what the Lord of lords says: Enough, rulers of Israel! Put away robbery and plunder, practice justice and righteousness, and lift your oppression from my people, says the Lord of lords.
You shall have honest scales, honest measures, and honest weights.
Regulate the measure and the weight so that you take tithes fairly, one part in ten.
The weights shall be twenty; a weight of them, twenty-five gerahs [?]; and a weight of fifteen shall be a mina for you.
This is the contribution you shall set apart: one-sixth of a cor of wheat and one-sixth of a cor of barley.
For oil, they shall take a tithe of one measure out of ten measures, which make a cor.
And one ewe out of every two hundred sheep of Israel shall be provided for the grain offering, the sacrifice, and the whole burnt offering, to purify them, says the Lord of lords.
All the people of the land shall set apart this contribution for the ruler of Israel.

The ruler shall be responsible for the whole burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the drink offerings at the new moons, on the Sabbaths, and at all the festivals of the house of Israel. He shall present the purification offering for sins, the grain offering, and the whole burnt offering—a sacrifice that purifies the people of Israel.
This is what the Lord of lords says: On the first day of the first month, take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.

The priest must take some of the blood of the purification offering and sprinkle it on the thresholds of the house, on the four corners of the altar, and on the threshold of the gate of the inner courtyard.
He shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who goes astray or errs, and they shall purify the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, you shall celebrate the Passover and the festival, and for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On that day the ruler shall offer a bull for purification from sins, on behalf of himself and all the people of the land.
During the seven days of the festival, he shall offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord: seven bulls and seven rams without defect, for purification from sins, and a male goat each day.
There shall be a seah of fine flour for each bull, a seah for each ram, and a hin of oil for each seah.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he shall celebrate the festival in the same way for seven days, with the same purification offerings for sins, the same whole burnt offerings, the same fine flour, and the same oil.

This is what the Lord of lords says: The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east shall remain closed during the six working days. On the Sabbath it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

The ruler shall enter from outside through the entrance at the threshold of the gate and stand at the gate's threshold. The priests shall offer his whole burnt offerings and his offerings. He shall bow down at the threshold of the gate and go out, and the gate shall not be closed until evening.
The people of the land shall bow down before the Lord at the entrance of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
The whole burnt offerings that the ruler offers before the Lord on the Sabbath shall be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect.
He shall provide a seah of fine flour for each bull, a seah for each ram, and as much as he can afford for each lamb, with a hin of oil for each seah.
On the day of the new moon, there shall be a bull without defect, six lambs without defect, and a ram without defect.
He shall provide a seah of fine flour for each bull, a seah for each ram, and as much as he can afford for each lamb, with a hin of oil for each seah.
When the ruler enters, he shall enter by the threshold of the gate and go out by the same way.

When the people of the land come before the Lord at festival time, whoever enters through the north gate to worship must leave through the south gate, and whoever enters through the south gate must leave through the north gate. No one must return through the gate by which they entered, but must leave through the opposite one.
The ruler who is among them shall go out through the gate by which he entered.
At the time of the festival, there shall be a seah of fine flour for a bull and a seah for a ram; for a lamb, each person shall give according to what he can afford, and a hin of oil for each seah.

When the ruler offers whole burnt offerings or offerings as a voluntary gift to the Lord, the closed gate facing east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his whole burnt offerings and his offerings, and they shall close the gate. Then he shall go out, as he does on the Sabbath.
Every day, morning after morning, he shall offer a year-old lamb without defect as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.

With it, morning after morning, he shall offer one-sixth of a seah of fine flour and one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, for the Lord. This is a lasting law, to be observed continually.
They shall offer the lambs, the fine flour, and the oil morning after morning as a continual whole burnt offering.
This is what the Lord of lords says: When the ruler gives a gift to one of his sons, his inheritance shall belong to his sons.

When he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall belong to the servant until the year of release, and then it shall belong to the ruler. But his sons' inheritance shall remain theirs.

The ruler shall not take any of the people's inheritance or wrongfully dispossess them of their property. Instead, he shall give his sons an inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people are driven from their own property.
He brought me through the entrance beside the gate into the inner hall of the priests' sanctuary, which faced north. I saw that there was a place there at its far western end.

He said to me, "This is the place where the priests boil the purification offerings for sins and bake the fine flour, so that they do not bring them out into the outer courtyard and make the people holy."
He brought me out into the outer courtyard and led me around its four sides. I saw a courtyard at one side of the courtyard and another courtyard at another side of the courtyard.
On the four sides of the courtyard were small courtyards, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide.
And colonnades surrounded all four of them.
He said to me, “This is the kitchen where the servants of the temple cook the people's sacrifices.”

He brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing out from beneath the eastern threshold of the temple. The water was flowing down from the side of the temple, south of the altar.
He brought me out through the northern gate and led me around outside to the gate of the courtyard that faces east. I saw water flowing out from its right side.
As the glorious man went out with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits and led me through water reaching to my ankles.
He measured a thousand cubits and led me through water reaching to my knees. He measured a thousand cubits and led me through water reaching to my waist.
He measured a thousand cubits: a stream that no one could cross, because the water had increased and the stream had grown strong, and no one could cross it.
He said to me, “Do you see, son of man?” Then he led me and seated me on the bank of the stream.
As I sat, I saw a great many trees on the bank of the stream, on both sides.
He said to me, “This water flows out to Galilee in the east, goes down to the north, and enters the sea, into its foul waters, and the waters become fresh.
Every living creature that reproduces will live wherever the water of the stream is. There will be many fish because of that water that flows in there, and the waters will become fresh.
Fishermen will stand beside it, from En-gedi to En-eglaim. It will be a place for spreading nets, and there will be many fish in it, like those of the Great Sea.
Its outlets and inlets will not become fresh, but will remain salt.

Along the stream, on its banks on both sides, every kind of food-bearing tree will sprout. Their leaves will not fall, and their fruit will not run out. At the beginning of every month they will bear fresh fruit, because the water they drink flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing.”
This is what the Lord of lords says: “The boundary allotments [?] by which the land is to be inherited are for the twelve tribes of Israel, with a portion for Joseph.
You are to inherit it, each with his brothers, for I raised my hand in an oath to give it to your ancestors. The land will be divided among you as an inheritance.
This is the boundary of the land on the north: from the Great Sea, along the road to Hethlon that leads to Zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, which lies between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath, and Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
The boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enan, on the border of Damascus, and Zaphon to the north, on the border of Hamath. This is the northern side.
On the eastern side, between Hauran and Damascus, and between Gilead and the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the boundary as far as the eastern sea of Tamar. This is the eastern side.
The southern side runs from Tamar as far as the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the inheritance of the Great Sea [?].
It forms the boundary as far as the point opposite the entrance to Hamath. This is the western side.
You shall divide this land among the tribes of Israel.

When you divide it as an inheritance for yourselves and for those who turn to me, who live among you and have had children among you, they will be like the Israelites. They will share the inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel.
In the tribe where someone who turns to me lives, there you are to give him an inheritance, says the Lord of lords.

These are the names of the tribes: from the northern end, along the road of Hethlon, at the entrance to Hamath and Hazar-enan, and the boundary of Damascus to the north beside Hamath—this is the side east of the sea belonging to Dan.
Along the border of Dan, from the eastern side to the western side, is Asher's portion.
Along the border of Asher, from the eastern side to the western side, is Naphtali's portion.
Along the border of Naphtali, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Manasseh’s portion.
Along the border of Manasseh, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Reuben’s portion.
Along the border of Reuben, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Judah’s portion.

Along the border of Judah, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be the contribution that you set apart, twenty-five thousand wide and as long as one of the portions, from the eastern side to the western side. The sanctuary shall be within it.
The contribution that you set apart for the Lord shall be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.

The sacred contribution shall belong to the priests: twenty-five thousand on the north, with a width of ten thousand; ten thousand on the west; ten thousand on the east; and twenty-five thousand on the south. The Lord’s sanctuary shall be within it.
It shall belong to the consecrated priests among the descendants of Zadok, who kept my instructions and did not go astray as the Israelites went astray and as the Levites went astray.
They shall have a contribution from the contribution of the land, a most holy portion adjoining the territory of the Levites.

The Levites shall have a portion alongside the territory of the priests, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. Their entire territory shall be twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.
They shall not sell any of it or exchange it, nor shall they transfer the first portion of the land, because it is holy to the Lord.
The five thousand that remain along the twenty-five thousand shall be an area for the city, for homes and open land. The city shall be within it.

These shall be its measurements: four thousand five hundred on the northern side, four thousand five hundred on the east, four thousand five hundred on the south, and four thousand five hundred on the west.
The city’s open land shall extend two hundred fifty to the north, two hundred fifty to the south, two hundred fifty to the east, and two hundred fifty to the west.

What remains alongside the sacred contribution, ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, shall lie alongside the sacred contribution. Its produce shall be food for those who work for the city.
Those who work for the city shall be drawn from all the tribes of Israel.
The entire contribution shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. Set apart the sacred contribution from the city’s allotted property.

What remains shall belong to the ruler of the city: from the sacred contribution and the city’s allotted property to the eastern border, along the twenty-five thousand, and to the west, along the twenty-five thousand at the western border, corresponding to the ruler’s portion. The sacred contribution and the sanctuary of the temple shall be within it.
Beyond the Levites’ allotted property and the city’s allotted property, the ruler’s portion shall be in the city, between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.
As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern side to the western side shall be Benjamin’s portion.
Along the border of Benjamin, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Simeon’s portion.
Along the border of Simeon, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Issachar’s portion.
Along the border of Issachar, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Zebulun’s portion.
Along the border of Zebulun, from the eastern side to the western side, shall be Gad’s portion.
Along the border of Gad, on the southern side, the boundary shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and its allotted territory shall extend to the Great Sea.
This is the land that you shall divide as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, says the Lord of lords.
These are the exits of the city: on the northern side, the measurement shall be four thousand five hundred.
And the gates of the city are named after the tribes of the Israelites. On the north are three gates: one for Reuben, one for Judah, and one for Levi.
And on the east, the measurement is 4,500, with three gates: one for Joseph, one for Benjamin, and one for Dan.
And on the south, the measurement is 4,500, with three gates: one for Simeon, one for Issachar, and one for Zebulun.
And on the west, the measurement is 4,500, with three gates: one for Gad, one for Asher, and one for Naphtali.
Its perimeter shall be eighteen thousand, and the name of the city from that time on shall be “The Lord Is There.”
